segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: As we begin, what is your English name?

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.translation: Janet K. Kirk Navarro.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: How about in Cherokee?

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.translation: Tsiyvn(i)sd(i).

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Tsiyvn(i)sd(i).

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.translation: Yes, Tsiyvn(i)sd(i).

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Where were you born?

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.translation: Tahlequah.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Tahlequah. Whereabouts did you grow up?

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.translation: Cherry Tree.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Cherry Tree. Your family?

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.text: ᎡᎵᏏ ᎡᏚᏗ ᎬᏩᏛ.ᎯᏍᏔᏅ ᎠᏯ, ᎡᏙᏓ ᏧᏲᎱᏒ ᏅᎩᏭ ᏯᏩᏕᏘᏴᏓ ᏥᎨᎲ
segments.translation: My grandma and grandpa raised me. When my dad died, I was just four years old.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: How many were you all in the family?

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.text: uh...ᎡᏥᏛ ᏚᏂᎧᎲ ᎣᏥᎧᎵ ᎨᎲ ᏅᎩᏭ ᏃᏥᎥ ᎠᏎᏃ there’s two more ᎠᏂᎠᏰᏟ ᎤᏍᏗᎧᏂ ᏃᏭᎴ ᎤᏔᏂᏓ,
segments.translation: Mom and Dad’s kids, we were full with only four kids but, there’s two more. They are only half siblings. The youngest and the oldest.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Did all of you all speak Cherokee?

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: I forgot her name, the teacher at Stilwell.

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.translation: Gina.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Gina, yeah. Is she your cousin?

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.translation: Yeah, that’s my oldest daughter.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᏂᎯᏛ ᏤᏥ...alright. ᎾᎮᏅ ᎥᎩᎵᏏ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏚᏪᏲᎲᏍᎬ ᎨᎵᎡ ᏣᏗ
segments.translation: Oh, that’s your child? Alright. My granddaughter, that will be her teacher.

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.translation: Is she learning well?

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Eh… she doesn’t try to learn.

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.text: ᏌᏊ ᏳᏩᎦᏓ ᏥᏫᏥᏫᏛ.ᎯᏙᎸ “ᎡᎵᏭᏍ ᏱᏪ.Ꮣ?” ᏧᏛᏅ “ᏙᏭᏅ?” ᏥᏲᎮᎸ ᏣᏛ.ᎪᏗᏃ ᎠᏩᏚᎵ ᎠᏂᏬᏂᏍᎬ ᏴᎨᎯᎵᏃᎮᏓ ...in Ꮎ fluent ᏣᎾᏗᎰ and then the learner...ᎤᏚᎵᎲ ᎤᎾᏕᎳᎰᎯᏍᏗ the difference, I guess...Ꮭ ᎢᎸᎯᏳ ᏱᎦᏥᏲᎵᏤᎮᎴ ᎢᎦᏓ and uh... “ᏙᎲ ᏍᎩᏳᏍᏗ ᏥᏕᎮᏲᎲᏍᎩ?” ᏥᏲᎮᎲ “ᏍᎩᏛ ᏂᎬᏁᏗ ᏗᎨᏲᏗ ᏃᏭᏅ ᏳᏭᎾᏕᏠᏆ ᎠᏃᎰᏅᏗ ᏍᏗ ᏃᏭᏅ ᏂᎯ ᏥᏂᏥᏪ ᏥᏥᏬᏂᎯ ᏳᏩᏟᎶᎦ” ᏧᏛᏅ
segments.translation: She asked if I would go over there and listen to them speak, and I then could speak to them – fluent and then a learner – they wanted to know the difference, I guess. I didn’t really understand some of them. “What are you teaching it like that?” I asked her. “That’s how you do it. And when they learn, they drop it a little bit. And then they’ll be speaking like you all.”

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᎠᏯᎮᎾ ᏯᎩᏁᎢᏍᏔᎾ ᎥᏍᎩᎾ Ꮵ.ᏃᎮᎲ ᏕᏗᏂᏕᏍᎪ ᎮᎾ ᎠᏯ ᏱᏗᏬᏂᎭ
segments.translation: When I mention what you are saying, we call it like “cutting a tail off.”

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.translation: Slang.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: We don’t pronounce all the words completely.

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.translation: No.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᏍᎩᎾ ᏳᏍᏗ ᎨᎨᏲᎲᏍᎪ ᏓᎾᏕᎶᏆ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎢᎦᏓ Ꮭ ᏳᎾᏁᎵ,ᏔᏃ ᎾᎮᏃ ᏥᏥᏃᎮ ᎥᎩᎵᏏ ᎮᏍᏗ ᎮᎾ Ꮭ ᎢᎸᎯᏳ ᎠᏆᎦ,Ꮫ.ᎦᏅ ᏱᎩ “ᎯᎠ ᏳᏍᏗ ᎦᏕᏠᎩ” ᎠᏗᎲ ᎾᏯᎥᎾᏭ ᏱᎩ ᏃᏭ Ꮭ ᏯᏩᎾᏔ...ᏝᎮᎾ Ᏺ...ᏧᎶᏒ Ᏺ...
segments.translation: That’s how they are taught, and that’s how they’re going to learn it. Some don’t try to learn it, because my granddaughter, who I was talking about, I have never heard her say, “This is what I learned.” And then she may not be in that class, I don’t know. What she’s been through...

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.text: ᎠᏂᏔᎵᏛ ᏥᎨᎲ and uh...Lawrence [Panther]...ᏥᏓᏕᏲᎲᏍᎬ ᏍᏊ...and he just, I guess he went to uh, the university .... ᏧᏑᎵᎪᏨ ᎾᎯᏳᏃ ᏂᎦᏓ ᏗᏂᏲᏟ...ᏥᏓᏥᎧᏁᎶᏅ Ꮎ ᎠᎨᏳᏣ ᏧᏪᏲᏗ. ᎢᎦᏛ Ꮭ ᏱᎩ ᏳᎾᎾᏖᏭ ᏣᏗᎲ ᏂᎦᏗᏅ ᏃᏭ ᎯᎠ ᏗᏢ ᏗᎦᏥᏍᏛᏡᏍᏗ ᏄᎵᏍᏔᏅ classes...ᏗᎦᏥᏰᏲᏗ ᏛᏓᎴᏂᏍᎬ ᏣᏗᎲ
segments.translation: There were two of them. And Lawrence [Panther], he was teaching too, and he went to the university when he quit. And when he left, they gave all of his students to her to teach. She said some of them didn’t really know. She said I had to put all of them on one side to teach them.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Ah. Some of them they really pick it up.

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.translation: Yes. They really talk to me when they see me now.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: What was it like as you all were growing up?

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.translation: What do you mean? My life?

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Just when you all were kids...

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.text: ᏙᏱᏛ ᏙᏣᏁᎶᎲᏍᎩ ᎨᎲ ᏂᎪᎸ ᏧᎾᏔᎾ ᎠᏁᏙ...ᎠᏁᏙᎲ ᏱᎩ ᎯᎠ ᏂᏣᏛᏁᏕᎨᏍᏗ ᏃᏊᎴ ᏂᎪᎸ ᏣᎳᎩᎭ ᏍᏓᏱ ᎮᎾ ᏙᎦᏛ.Ꮢ and uh....ᏃᏭ Momma ᏃᏭ ᎤᏍᎦᏅᏥᎶᎥ...ᏥᏙᎩᏯᏅᎲ...ᏐᏁᎳᏛᎡ ᏍᎪᎯ ᎴᏱᎩᏢ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏯᏩᏕᏘᏴᏓ ᏃᏭᏅ State ᏧᎾᏕᎶᏆᏍᏗ ᏃᏭ boarding school ᏥᏙᎦᏛ.Ꮢ
segments.translation: We always played outside, and the parents were nearby talking Cherokee. Then we grew up poor, but we always talked Cherokee. And mama she was running around, and the state took us away, I was about 9 or 10 years old. We grew up at the boarding school.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Where was it?

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.translation: At first, Eufala.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Huh!

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.text: ᎠᏂᎨᏳᏣ ᏂᎦᏓ ᏣᏂᏯᎥ ᎾᏅ ᎠᏧᏣ ᏃᏭ ᏗᏕᎶᏆᏍᏗ ᏥᏄᎵᏍᏔᏂᏢ one yearᏭ ᏧᏬᎩᏴᏢ ᏃᏭ Seneca ᏗᏢ ᏥᏃᎦᏛᏂᏔᏅ
segments.translation: There were only girls in the building. And the boy, when he got old enough to go to school, we were only there one year and then they sent us to Seneca.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Did you all want to go there on your own?

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.translation: We had to go.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Y’all had to go.

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.text: ᏧᏚᎵᎲ ᎮᎾ ᎡᎵᏏ Ꮶ-ᎣᎦᎦᏎᏍᏙᏗ “ᏱᎬᎩᏍᏕᎵᏅ Ᏺ” cause...ᎡᏚᏗ ᎮᏅ Ꮭ ᏯᏩᎾᏔ ᏦᏍᎪ gap ᎨᎲ ᏚᎾᏕᏘᏱᏍᎬ ᎡᎵᏏ and... “ᏱᎬᎩᏍᏕᎵᏙᎸ Ᏺ” ᏧᏛᏅ
segments.translation: My grandma wanted to keep us “They would have been helping me,” [she said.] Grandpa, I don’t know, a 30-year gap between their ages. She said “They would’ve been helping me.”

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Let me ask you this, who were your grandparents?

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.translation: Me?

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Yes.

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.text: ᎠᏴᏍᏗ ᏥᏚᏙᎥ ᎡᎵᏏ, ᎤᏂᎧᎲ and uh... Livers ᎦᏙ.Ꭹ ᎤᏪᎸ and uh... and then Elsie Seabolt Ꮎ ᏥᎬᏲᎮᎲ ᎡᏙᏓᏅ ᎨᎲ ᎺᎵ, -Maggie Daugherty ᎤᏥ ᎨᎲ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎡᏙᏓ, - Felix Kirk.
segments.translation: Me. Vyvsd(i) was his name, Els(i)’s kid. And Livers Gatog(i) Uwelv and then Els(i) Seabolt, as I was telling you. And my dad, Mel(i) was her name, Maggie Daugherty was his mom. And her dad was Felix Kirk.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᏏᏍ ᎥᎾ uh...Dahlonegah ᎾᎥᏂᎨᏍᏗ ᏏᏍ ᎥᎾ ᎯᏁᎳ?
segments.translation: Do you still live near Dalonegeh?

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.text: Uh huh. ᎾᏛ ᎠᎦᏴᎵᎨᏃ “ᎠᎦᏴᎵᎨ” ᏱᏥᏲᎮᎳ, ᏴᎩᏐᎮᎴ uh...ᏗᏲᎤᏟ ᎮᎾ ᎤᏍᏗᎧᏂ ᎤᏂᎧᎲ ᎨᎲ ᏂᎪᎯᎸ ᎯᎠ wheelchair ᏧᏣᏅ ᏃᏭᏅ ᎠᏯ ᎣᏂ ᎤᎾ ᏫᎨᏙᎲ...all day...ᏙᎩᏃᏠ ᏥᎦᏎᏍᏙ...she’s 78.
segments.translation: Uh huh. I still live there. The old lady—If I had called her “old lady” she would have probably gotten onto me. The youngest was crippled, he was always in a wheelchair, and I was there all day watching him. She’s 78.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Oh.

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.text: Yeah. ᎠᏎᏃ ᏃᏭ...you can tell now...ᏩᏅ,ᎦᎶ ᏂᎦᎵᏍᏗᎭ
segments.translation: Yeah, but now you can tell she was getting weak.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: How many children do you have?

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.translation: Me? Two.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Two.

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.translation: They’re girls.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Do they speak Cherokee?

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.text: ᎤᏔᏂᏓ ᎤᏩᏌ ᎤᏙᏓ,Ꮫ ᏤᎲ ᎤᏍᏗᎧᏂ ᎠᎫᏐ ᎮᎾ ᎨᎲ “ᎠᏯᏛ ᎯᎾ ᏓᏥᏰᏲᏂ,” ᏧᏛᏅ ᏙᏳ ᏓᎨᏲᎲᏍᎬ ᎠᎫᏐ ᎤᏬᏂᎯᏍᏗ Ꮳ,ᎦᏍᏗᏛ ᏱᎾᏂᏫ ᏥᎨᎲ
segments.translation: Just the older one. When her dad was alive, the younger one, he was a Creek. He said he was going to teach her to speak Creek. He was really teaching her, and they could really speak well.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: She was speaking?

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.translation: Yeah, she forgot all of it.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: What was her name?

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.translation: Her dad or the girl?

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.translation: Stephanie.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Stephanie.

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.translation: I thought you knew her.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Yes, I have to ask you.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: [laughter]

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.text: Oh, okay. [ᎤᏰᏣᏍᎦ] ᎾᎾ...ᎠᏎᏅ ᎤᏮᎨᏫ,ᏐᏅ ᏂᎦᏓ Ꮟ ᎠᏅᏓᏗᏍᎪ.
segments.translation: Oh, [laughs] but she forgot it all, but she remembers all of it.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: She forgot the Creek?

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: She didn’t pick up Cherokee?

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.translation: If I get onto to her, she understands.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: [laughs]

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᎠᏬᎯᏳᏛ ᎩᎶ--ᏍᎩᏭ ᏱᎨᎮ ᏱᎪᎵ,Ꭶ ᏱᎦᏐᎮᎳ Um....Ꮝ-ᏍᎩᏃᎯᏏ ᎾᎲ ᏄᏍᏛ ᏕᏣᏛ.Ꮢ ᏄᏍᏛ ᏗᏣᎶᏒ ᏗᏣ-ᏗᏥᏲᏟ ᏥᎨᎲ
segments.translation: I think anybody would understand if somebody got onto them. Tell me how you all were as children and how you grew up.

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.text: Okay. ᎠᏯᏛ ᏃᏭ...I’m 66...ᏃᏭ ᏑᏓᎵᏍᎪᎯ ᏑᏓᎵ ᎾᏩᏕᏘᏱ ᎦᏅᏓᏗᏍᎪ ᎡᏙᏓ Ꮟ...just like...ᏒᎯᏭ ᏱᏄᎵ,ᏍᏔᏅ...and he’s always stayed...ᏥᏓᏅᏖᏍᎬ ᎤᏓᏂᏖᏅ ᎨᎲ ᏂᎬ. ᏨᎩ,ᏘᏂᏙ ᎦᏅᏓᏗᏍᎪ ᏦᎩ,ᏍᏗᎩᏁ ᎨᎮ ᎨᎵᎰ ᏱᏙᎩᎾᏅᏍᏓ ᏥᎨᎲ car-Ꭲ ᎠᎬᏱ ᏱᏬᎩᏗᎲ ᏙᏳ ᎠᎧ MamaᏃ ᏱᏩᏥᏯᏅ ᏯᎦᏍᎬ ᏣᎦᏍᎬ ᏌᏭ ᏳᏩᎦᏓ ᎦᏅᏓᏗᏍᎪ ᏯᎫᏢ’Ꮫ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏱᏩᏥᏯᎥᎦ ᏃᏭ ᎡᎵᏏ ᏤᎲ ᏧᏁᏅᏒ...and they were happy I guess...Ꮭ ᏯᎩᏲᎱᏎ ᏃᏊᎴ slab ᏧᏄᏍᏗ Dahlonegah ᎦᎶᏐᏅ...
segments.translation: Okay. Me, I am 66. I still remember my dad like it was yesterday. He’s always stayed in my mind. He was real nice and I remember he took me places. I remember, I guess we were too small, a car would go by and he put us in a car. And then he came and got mom if it was raining. One time, when it was raining, I remember he put a cover on her and put her in the car at Grandma’s house. And they were happy I guess, and I didn’t forget. And slab, that’s there past Dalonegeh, you know.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Mm.

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.text: ᏣᎾᏔ ᎥᎾ ᏱᏩᎦᎶᎯᏍᏗ ᎨᎲ “ᏫᏣᏓᏬᏣ ᎥᎾ” Ꮳ,ᎦᏍᏗᏛ ᏙᏣᏓᏏᏂᏙ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎣᏍᏓ ᎦᏅᏓᏗᏍᎪ Ᏺ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏤᎲ ... ᏃᏭᏅ ᏥᏄᎵᏍᏔᏂᏙᎸ Mama ᎮᎾ ᎤᎯᏐᏓᏁᎴ ᎡᏙᏓ ᏧᏲᎱᏒ ᏃᏭᏅ ᏧᎵ ᎠᏂᎷᎬ ᏃᏭ y’know ᏄᏓᎴ ᏄᎵᏍᏔᏅ ᎠᏗᏔᏍᎬ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎤᏢ ᏧᏲᎱᏒ
segments.translation: And he would stop there and he would tell us to go swim. It was a good place. We would really be crawling around in the water. I remember him well, then. And then that happened. Mama was real sad when my dad died. When her friends started coming around, ya know, that’s when she changed. She was drinking and that’s what killed her.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Isn’t Ft. Gibson?

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.translation: Gadeyi,di.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᏍᎩᏛ ᎦᏕᏱ,Ꮧ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏙᎲᎡ ᎦᏅᏓᏗᏍᎪ ᎮᏅ Housing Authority ᏫᏓᎩᎸᏫ,ᏍᏓᏁᎲ ᏫᏥᏫ,Ꮫ.ᎯᏙᎲ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎪᏪᎵ ᎣᏍᏗᎧᎵᏏᎲ Ꮭ ᏍᏊ ᎢᎸᎯᏳ ᏯᏩᎾᏛ ᎫᏍᏗ ᏳᎾᏛᏁᎸ ya’know?
segments.translation: Gadeyi,di that’s what it was. I remember I was working at the Housing Authority. I used to go visit him and fill out papers. But I don’t know if they ever did anything.

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.translation: [laughs]

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.translation: He could talk mean.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᎯᎾ ᎬᏯᏛ.ᏛᏅᎢ um...ᏅᏃ ᎣᏍᏓ ᎾᏅᏁ ᎥᎾᏍ ᏂᎯᏴ ᏫᏛᎦᏛ.ᎴᏏ?
segments.translation: Let me ask you this; they are fixing the road, is it going to come out over there?

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.text: Umm...yeah, ᏂᎬᏅᎯᏒ all the way to ᎠᏂ-Proctor’s ᏗᏂᏁᎳ
segments.translation: Yeah, all the way to where the Proctors live.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Are they really going to black-top it?

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.translation: That’s what they said. They already got it ready to pave.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: Huh. ᎣᏍᏓ ᎨᎮᏍᏗ ᏙᎲ ᏍᎩ ᏥᎩ
segments.translation: It’s going to be good, isn’t it?

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᏙᎲ ᏍᎩ ᏙᎲ yeah. ᎤᏂᎪᏕᏍᏗ ᎴᏱᎦ ᎠᎾᏛᏁᎵᏍᎩ ᎨᎵᎰ ᎠᏯ Um...ᎭᏢ ᏕᏣᏕᎶᏆᎡ?
segments.translation: You’re probably right. There’ll probably be more mean characters going by. Where did you go to school?

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.text: ᏓᎶᏁᎨᏍᏛ ᏥᏓᏩᏕᎶᏆᎥ 4 years ᏃᏭ 5th grade ᏥᎾᎩᏴᏢ ᎾᎯᏳ ᏥᎨᏒ ᏦᎦᏂᎩᏒ
segments.translation: Dalonegeh sdv I went four years. When I was in fifth grade, that’s when we left.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: Eufala ᏫᏨᏅᎮᏅ ᏃᏭᏍ high school ᏱᎪᎯᏓ Seneca’s Ꮺ.Ꭾ?
segments.translation: Y’all went to Eufala. Were you in Seneca all through high school?

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.translation: Just eighth grade.

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.translation: When I finished eighth grade, I went to Sequoyah.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: You got to Sequoyah.

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.text: ᎥᎥ 3 years ᏱᎪᎯᏓ ᎥᎾ ᎣᏂ ᏕᏥᏍᏆᏗᏍᎬ ᎠᎩᎩᏐᏗᏅ ᎨᎲ ᎦᏳᎳ ᎡᎵᏏ “ᎠᎭᏂ ᏕᎭᏕᎶᏆᎥ Cave Springs ᎥᎾ ᏘᏍᏆᏗ,” ᏣᏬᎮᎸ “ᎡᎵᏍᏓ ᏱᏍᏉᎵᏍᏉᎳᏓᏏᏭ ᏫᏓᎩᏍᏆᏗᏍᏗ ᎠᎭᏂ? ᎾᎪᎯᎸ ᎦᏂᎦ” ᏥᏲᎮᎸ...but there was a time...ᏙᏳᏙ ...next to me...ᎠᎩ--ᏦᏍᏓᏓᎸ ᏂᎪᎯᎸ ᎮᏅ ᎥᎩ,ᏍᏓᏩᏗᏙ ᎨᎲ ᎠᏯ ᎡᎵᏏ ᎡᏚᏓ ᏂᎪᎯᎸ “ᏣᏓᎾᏘ ᎨᎮᏍᏗ ᎮᏍᏗ ᎢᎸᎯᏳ ᏣᏁᎫᏤᏍᏗ ᎢᎸᏢ ᎡᏣᏘᏁᎬ--ᎠᏁᎬ ᎮᎨᏍᏗ,” ᏯᏓ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎯᎪᏛ.ᎲᎢ...so Seneca...ᏥᏩᎩᎷᏨ after my 8th grade...Choctaw Central ᏥᏓᏩᏕᎶᏆᎥ Ꮎ ᎠᎨᏳᏣ ᏦᏍᏓᏓᎸ ᏣᎩ,ᏍᏓᏩᏕᏒ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎤᎯᏐᏓᏅ ᎤᎯᏓᏁᎲ ᏃᏊᎴ ᏙᎩᏁᏅᏒ
segments.translation: For three years. I was the last one to finish. I was already used to it, and Grandma told me to go finish school at Cave Springs. “Can you let me finish school where I’m at? I had already been gone so long,” I told her. But there was a time, the one next to me, my sister always followed me. My grandparents always told me to be good and never been mean when they take you somewhere. And when they go somewhere, go with them. So, you can see, when I got to Seneca after my eighth grade I went to school at Choctaw Central. And that girl, my sister, followed me, because she was lonely. And then we came back.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᏂᎦᏓᏍ ᎢᏥᎷᏨ Seneca ᎥᎾ ᏣᏂᎩᏒ ᏂᎦᏓ?
segments.translation: Did all of y’all come back from Seneca?

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.text: Mhm. ᏣᏅ,Ꮤ, Ᏺ ᏂᎦᏓ uh...Ꭳ-ya’know ᎣᎦᏓᏝᎬ ᏌᏊ “ᎮᏍᏗᏅ ᏥᏨᎨᏫ,Ꮟ ᏣᎳᎩ ᏥᏨᎨᏫ,Ꮟ” ᏧᎾᏛᏅ ᎮᏅ ᏙᎲ ᏥᏬᎩᎷᏨ ᏥᏙᎩᎨᏳᏗᎲ ᎣᎩᏬᏂᎯᏍᏗ Ꮭ ᏍᎩ ᎢᏳᏍᏗ ᎤᎦᎮᏗ ᏱᎨᎮ ᎡᎲ ᏥᏩᏩᎴᏅᎲ ᎤᎪᏗᏃ ᏣᎳᎩ ᎠᏂᏬᏂᏍᎩ ᏗᎾᎦᏎᏍᏗᏍᎩ ᏥᏚᏂᎸᏫᏍᏓᏁᎲ
segments.translation: Yeah. We were all there and we said not to forget Cherokee, but the school would not let us talk our language, but it wasn’t that bad. When we got there there were more workers there that spoke Cherokee.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Uh huh.

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.text: ᎠᏎᏃ ᎢᎸᏢ ᏓᏲᏥᏅ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏣᎳᎩᎭ ᎣᏥᏬᏂᏍᎬ ᏲᏣᏝᎮ
segments.translation: But we’d all be sitting somewhere, all of us speakers, talking.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: They really did tell you all quit talking Cherokee?

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: What did you think when they told you that?

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.text: “ᏙᎨ?” ᏱᎨᎵᏭ ᏥᎨᎲ hmm, but I did ᎠᏯ “Ꮭ” ᏧᏛᏅ ᎡᏚᏓ ᎦᏥᏲᎮᎲ ᏍᎩᏳᏍᏗ ᎣᏣᏓᏟᏏᎲ ᎤᏓᏩᏗᏍᎬ ‘ᎸᏢ ᏲᏥᏅ ᏥᎨᎲ
segments.translation: “Why?” I would think. But I did. “Grandpa told us not to [forget it],” I told them. We’d all be sitting somewhere in the shade talking.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: You all were talking?

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.text: ᎠᏎᏃ Ꭳ-Ꭳ-Ꭶ-ᎣᏣ...how would you say? We won.
segments.translation: But, how would you say? We won.

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.translation: [laughter]

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.text: ᏝᏃ ᎩᎶ ᏲᏣᏕᏙ.ᏗᎰ ᎣᏥᏬᏂᏍᎬ Simon Bush ᎮᏅ ᏥᏭᎷᏨ ᎠᏩᎵᎮᎵᏨ Ᏺ ᏙᎮᏅ ᎤᎪᏛ...ya’know like him..uh...what was that one’s name? ᏙᏳ ᎠᏂᏣᎳᎩ Kansas ᏚᎾᏂᎩᏓ ᏧᎾᎴᏅᎲ ᏚᏂᎸᏫᏍᏓᏁᎲ Ahh... Ms. Christie...
segments.translation: Nobody bothered us speaking our language. Simon Bush came as we were talking, we were all glad that they came because there were more now that was speaking the language. So like him and Miss Christie, they came from Kansas and started working there.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Did it become better?

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.text: Yes, ᎠᏯᏛ ᏂᎪᎯᎸ ᏣᎳᎩ ᏲᎦᏝᏃᎮᏗ ᏥᎨᎲ
segments.translation: Yes, she always talked to us in Cherokee.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᏝᎲ ᏙᏲ ᎠᏯ ᎮᏅ Northeastern ᏓᏩᏕᎶᏆᎥ Ꮎ uh... Chilocco ᏣᏃᎮ ...ᎦᎵᏉᎩᏛ ᏃᏥᎥ ᎣᎦᎵᏲᏕᎪ ᎨᎲ ᎠᏂᏍᎦᏯ ᎠᏯ ᏩᎩᏍᏗᎬ um...’ᎸᏢ ᎤᎾᏛᎦᏅ ᎩᎶ ᎢᏳᏍᏗ Chilocco ᏧᎸᏫᏍᏓᏁᎯ flashlight ᎬᏗ ᎤᎸᏂᎴ ᎠᏴᏫᏯ ᏗᏕᎶᏆᏍᎩ ᎥᎾ Chilocco ᎢᏕᏒᎯ ᎤᎾᏛᏅ ‘ᎸᏢ ᎣᎨᏅᏒ ᏒᏃᏱ ᎨᎲ ᏌᏭᎢᏛᏢ ᎠᏟᎢᎵᏒ ᏬᎩᎷᏨ ᏩᏥᏰᎢᏍᏔᏅ--ᏭᏂᏰᎢᏍᏔᏅ ᏄᎬᏫᏳᏒ
segments.translation: I went to school Northeast…the one they call Chilocco… There was about seven of us men always together and I was the smallest. They heard it somewhere that a Chilocco worker beat up a Cherokee student with a flashlight and they said, “Let’s go.” So we went and got there about one o’clock and we woke up the boss

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.translation: Oh gosh.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᎤᏂᎯᎵᏙᎸᏛ ᏞᎦ uh... “ᏏᏍᎪ ᏚᎸᏫᏍᏓᏁ?” ᎠᎪᎮᎴ “ᏏᏛ ᏚᎸᏫᏍᏓᏁ.” “ᏙᎨ?” ᏍᎩᏛ ᏍᏓᏱ ᎤᏂᎯᎵᏙᎸ ᏝᏍ Ᏺ ᏍᎩᏳᏍᏗ ᏂᎦᎵᏍᏔᏅᏍᎨ ᎥᎾ Seneca?
segments.translation: They had a meeting for a while. And they asked them if he still worked there, and he said he did. They really interrogated him harshly. Wasn’t that how it was at Seneca?

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.text: ᏣᏂᏃᎮᏍᎬᎡ ᏥᏩᎩᎷᏨ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏂᎦᎵᏍᏗᎲ Uh...ᏃᏊᎴ ᎠᎵᏍᏓᏴᏗ ᏱᎩ Ᏺ ᎠᎬᏱ ᏬᎦᎴᏅᎲ ᎣᎦᎴᏅᏛ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏣᎾᏓᏙᎵᏍᏗᎮ...and uh...ᎩᎳ ᏲᏣᎾᎥᎦ ᏳᏓᎭ ᏍᏊ Ꮭ ᏯᏩᎾᏔ ᏐᏈᎵ ᎭᏫᏯ ᏱᎬᎩᏁ I mean, I wonder ᏍᎩᎾ ᎭᏩᏯ ᎮᏅ ᏯᏅᏂᏍᏗ ᏥᎨᎲ Ꮩ ᎮᏅ PinkᎥᏭᏛ ᏱᎩ ᎠᎻᎭ Granny ᏂᎪᎸ “ᎮᏍᏗ ᏥᏣᏁᎵ,ᏓᏁᎮᏍᏗ ᏍᏗᏭ ᏍᏊ ᎯᎩᏍᎨᏍᏗ,” ᎠᎩᏄᎸᏅᏛ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏥᏈᏍᏗ ᏃᏒᎾ ᎤᎾ ᏍᎩ ᏱᎩ ᎦᏥᏲᎮᎸ ᏌᏊ ᏦᏍᏓᏓᎸ ᏣᎦᏍᏗᏛ ᏱᏅᎬᏁ ᏥᎨᎲ but...ᎾᎡ Granny ᏥᏥᏃᏎ--ᏥᎬᏃᏎᏅ ᏙᎡᏅ ᎣᎨᏲᏅ to fix the bed, be neat everyday and ᏃᏊᎴ ᎠᎹ ᏗᎫ.Ꭹ.ᏍᏗ pale the water ᎣᎦᏓᏬᏍᏗᏅ ᏱᎩ ᎤᏔᎾ tub ᏧᏩᏯ and ᎥᎾ ᏲᏥᎧᎵᏏ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏦᎢᏅ trees ᏥᏕᎨᏚᏒᏛᏕ ᎥᎾ curtain sheets ᏱᏕᎦᏛᎥᎦ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎥᎾ ᏲᏣᏓᏬᏣ,
segments.translation: They were talking about it when we got there. When it was time to eat, we had to stand up front and then they would pray. And then after that we could sit down. One time I really thought I was eating horse meat. I mean I really wondered what kind of meat it was. It was really pink and Grandma always told us to go ahead and eat, even just a little bit. I couldn’t eat it. “A lot wasn’t good over there,” I told them. My sister really did eat hers. I was telling you about granny, they really taught us to fix the bed and be neat every day and also to get water when we had to take a bath. She had a big tub. We would fill it up and she would hang sheets up on three trees and we would take a bath.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: At y’all’s home?

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.text: Mhm. ᎠᎹᏛ ᎡᎬ ᎾᎥ And uh...the..Ꮎ ᏗᏂᏲᏟᎡ ᎠᏯ ᏣᎩᎵᏏ ᎪᎱᏍᏗ ᏧᎵ,ᏍᏔᏂᏙᎸ ᎠᎹ ᏧᏲᏨ “’Ꮩ ᏓᏓᏛᏁᎵ?” ᏧᎾᏛᏅᏛ “Come with me,” ᎦᏥᏲᎮᎸ ᎠᏭᎨ ᏫᏕᏓ ᎾᏛ ᎠᎹ ᎡᎦ ᏬᎩᎷᏨ Ꮎ lawnchair ᎠᏬᏢ “ᎯᎡ ᏂᏣᏛᏁᏗ ᏍᎩ ᏱᏄᎵ,ᏍᏔᏅ ᏙᎦᏛᏌ” ᎥᎾᏛ ᏂᎦᏓ ᏙᎦᎵ,ᏍᏚᎴᎲ ᎢᎦᏓᏅ ᎤᏪᏴ Ꮎ ᎡᎬ ᏍᏗ ᎣᏏ ᎥᎾᏛ ᏙᏧᏃᏢ ᎠᎾᏓᏬᏍᎬ ᎠᎾᏓ--ᎾᎾ ᏝᎮᎾᏲ ᏦᎦᎿᏪᏍᏗ ᏱᎩᏃ ᏕᏥᏄᏩ ᏩᏩᏓᏅᎦᎵ ᏥᏲᎮᎲ ᏍᎩᏭ ᎾᎾᏛᏁᎲ ᎠᏎᏃ ᎦᏁᎵ,ᏗᎰ ᎦᏥᏰᏲᏗ ᎪᎯᏗᎮᎾ ᏥᎦᏘᏱ,Ꮧ ᎨᎵᎣ
segments.translation: Yeah. There was water running nearby. And my grandkids—something happened to the water—they said, “What’re we going to do now?” “Come here,” I told them. We went to where the water was running and I was sitting in a lawn chair and I told them, “This is what you all need to do when this happens.” This is what we did. I told them all, “Let’s just wash our hair in the creek.” They were sitting the water, one that was with us I told them that they didn’t have to take their clothes off to clean up. “Just clean up with your clothes on,” I told them. I try to teach them as long as I am here.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: They don’t like to play outside.

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.text: Mmmm...ᎾᏛ ᏂᎦᏓ ᏧᎾᏔᎾ ᎾᏂᏪᏍᎬ ᎠᏎᏃ ᏓᏐᎮᎰ Ꮎ ᎠᎨᏳᏣ ᎩᎳ ᎢᎪᎯᏓ ᏙᏳ ᏱᏫ,ᎨᏥᎨ.ᎯᏓ ᏳᎦᎾᏩ
segments.translation: Yes, and they know that, but they are told to go outside. That girl gets onto them, she runs them outside real quick.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᎠᏯᏅ ᎮᏍᏗ ᎠᏎ ᎡᎩᎨᎯᏓᏍᏗ ᏱᎨᎮ ᏙᎲ?
segments.translation: They didn’t really have to chase us out, ain’t it?

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.text: Huh uh. ᏣᎾᏔ ᏱᏙᎩᏲᏏ ᎮᎾ ᎡᎵᏏ ᏥᏈᏍᏗ ᎦᏚ ᏱᏕᎬᏂᏍᏓ ᏥᎨᎲ...and uh...ᏲᎩᏲᏏᏅ Ꮎ ᏒᎩ ᏱᏬᏥᎾ,ᏌᏁᎦ ᏥᎨᎲ Ᏺ ᏱᏬᏥᏅᎦᎳ ᏃᏊᎴ ᏥᏍᏛᎾ ᎠᏂᏯᎥ ᎥᎾ ᎤᏪᏴ ᎠᎹ...uh...ᎥᎾ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏱᏙᏥᏂᏯ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏣᎦᏍᏗᏛᏅ Ꮎ ᎠᏓ stove ᎦᎧᎲ ᎥᎾ ᎡᏙᏓ ᏧᏮᏂᏍᏗ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏍᎩᏭ biscuit-Ꭲ or mustard-ᎢᏭ ᎴᏱᎦ ᎤᏩᏍᏚᏢ ᏏᎦᏭ ᏲᏣᏓᏬᎠ ᎤᏙᏓᏩᏓ,
segments.translation: You know it. When we were hungry, Granny, she would make a whole bunch of bread. When we were hungry, we would go pull up a lot of onion and fix it and also there were crawdads in the creek. We would catch a whole bunch of them, and there was a wood stove there, where dad would cook them. We had biscuits with mustard on it and onion and crawdad. We would swim all day.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: [laughs]

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: What did you say? Mustard?

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.text: Mustard and biscuit [claps hands together] ᎦᏅᎵᏰ ᏥᏍᏛᎾ ᏒᎩᏅ
segments.translation: Mustard and biscuit… and crawdad and onion.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: “Asutlv” is what you said, right?

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.translation: Huh?

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Or did I misunderstand you?

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.translation: Uh...probably.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: The reason I ask is because...

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.translation: Or did you say “ganvliyedi” [to rub onto something]

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.translation: Oh, ganvliyedi

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᏍᎩᏛ ᏙᎲ ᎠᏩᎾᏔ ᏍᎩᏳᏍᏗ ᏂᎨᎲ Ᏺ....ᎩᎳ ᎮᏅ
segments.translation: That’s what it was, ain’t it. I know what that is. When I hear a word I don’t recognize, I write them down.

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.translation: Oh really? Huh.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: Um....ᏗᎨᏣᎦ--ᏗᎨ--ᏗᎨᏣᎵ--ᏣᎵᏏ ᏗᎨᏣᏚᏚᎢᏅ ᎨᏒ ᎾᎥᏍ ᏂᏣᏍᏕ--ᏍᎩᏍ ᎤᎬᏫᏳ ᏥᏕᎨᏣᏛ.ᎯᏍᏔᏁ?
segments.translation: Your grannies and grandpas, were they nearby or were they the ones that raised you?

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.translation: Just me by myself.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Just you.

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.text: ᎠᏂᏐ ᎮᏅ Ꮭ ᏯᏩᎾᏔ ᎯᏲᎵᎦ ᏱᎦ Ꮎ ᏐᎢ uh...ᎬᏃ ᎠᏃᎮᎲ ᏥᎨᎲ
segments.translation: The others, I don’t know if you know him, Gvno they call him. He had to take us in, but he was mean sometimes. I didn’t like it. That’s why I left.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Gvno yeah, yeah.

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.text: ᏍᎩ ᎮᏅ ᏦᎩᏯᎾ ᏥᏄᎵ,ᏍᏔᏅ ᎣᎣ ᎠᏎᏃ ᎤᏁᎫᏥᏛ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏳᏓᎭ ᏍᎩᎾ Ꮭ ᏯᎩᎸᏉ,ᏔᏁ ᎠᏯ
segments.translation: He had to take us in but he was mean sometimes. I didn’t like it.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Mm.

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.translation: That’s not what I was taught. So, I left.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Did he drink too?

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.text: Huh uh. ᏱᎨᎵ Ꮭ ᏯᏩᎾᏔ ᏳᏓᎭ ᎴᏱᎦ ᏱᎨᏛ.ᏍᎦ ᏱᎨᎵ But uh...ᏃᏭᏅ ᎡᎵᏏ ᏧᏁᏅᏒ ᏣᏪᏅᏒ “ᎠᏎᏗᎲ ᎥᏤᏅᏍᏗ.” ᏥᎬᏬᎮᎸ “ᏱᏫᎨᎾᏛ” ᏥᏥᏲᎮᎸ ᎠᏎᏃ ᏔᎵᏁ Ꮵ-ᏥᎶᏒ ‘ᏚᏚ ᎮᏅ ᏂᎪᎸᏛ Porch-Ꭲ ᏳᏬᏢ ᏥᎨᎲ “Ꮒ, ᎡᎵᏏ! ᎡᎵᏏ ᎾᎢ Whoo!” ᏱᏛᏬᏌ ᏥᎨᎲ And ᏂᎬ ᎮᏅ ᎤᏅᎦᎸᎰᏅ ᏂᎨᎲ--ᏥᎨᎲ ᎥᎾ EᏩᎪᏛᏗ “Haw!” ᏱᎨᎵᏛ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎠᏩᏓᏂᏴᏓ ᎾᎩᏰᎸ ᎠᏯ but uh...ᏃᏭ ᏍᏊ ᏥᏄᎵ,ᏍᏔᏅ ᏧᎷᏨ case worker “ᎯᎠᏛ ᎠᎨᏳᏣ ᎠᏩᏚᎵ ᎠᏯ ᎠᏩᏝᏫᏍᏙᏗ” ᏧᏛᏅ ᏙᏳᏃ ᎥᎾ ᏣᏩᏛ.Ꮢ
segments.translation: No, I don’t think so. And then he might stand the bottle up sometimes. That’s when I went back to my grandma, but they kept telling me I had to go back. I said I would go back, but when I would pass by, Grandpa used to sit outside all the time. He would tell Grandma that I was walking by, would just hoop at me. He would have it all cleaned up, you could see it, and I would think, “Haw, I thought I had just left this place.” But then a case worker showed up and they said, “I want this girl to come live with me.” And that’s where I grew up.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: And Julio Pritchett? What was he to you?

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.text: He’s ᎬᏃᏛ ᎤᏪᏥ ᏍᎩᎾ... first cousin.
segments.translation: He’s Gvnod’s son. He was my first cousin.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: We both learned at Cave Springs.

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.translation: Oh you? Wow.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: Ꮭ...Ꮭ same grade ᏱᎨᎮ ᎠᎬᏱ ᏣᎢᏎ ᎠᏎᏃ ᏍᎩᎾ--
segments.translation: Not in the same grade, he was a grade ahead of me…

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.translation: He was really nice.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: --ᏂᎪᎯᎸ ᎣᎦᎵᏲᏕᎬ ᏥᎨᎲ Cave Springs ᏦᎦᏕᎶᏆᎥ ᏙᏳ ᎤᎵᏲᏗᏛ ᏥᎨᎲ
segments.translation: We ran around together when we went to school at Cave Springs. He was a cry baby.

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.text: ᏌᏭ ᏳᏩᎦᏓ ᏥᏣᏁᏙᎲ ᎠᏓᏁᎸ...at granny’s...porch-Ꭲ ᏧᏂᎩ.Ꮈ WoodrowᎢᏍ ᎯᏲᎵᎦ ᎨᎮ?
segments.translation: [laughs] One time they were at the house on the porch and – did you know Woodrow?

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Woodrow, that lived...?

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.translation: Okay.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Yeah, yeah.

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.text: Ꮎ roadrunner ᎮᏅ ᏥᏈᏍᏗ ᏳᎾ--ᏳᎾᏛᏁ,Ꮧ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏅᏯ Ꭼ,ᏗᎲ ᏥᏓᏳᎩ.Ꮈ ᎠᏂᏧᏣ ᏓᏂᏍᏓᏲᎯᎲ ᎠᏎᏃ Ꮭ ᏯᏂᎯᎮᎡ ᎾᎥᏭ ᎮᏅ ᎯᎢᏭ ᎾᏛᏁᎲ...y’know...ᎠᏛᏁᏏᏙᎲ. “Hmm!,” ᎤᏛᏅᏛ Julio and uh...”ᎠᏯᏅ ᎦᏁᎵ,Ꮧ!” ᎠᎪᎮᎸ Woodrow ᏫᏓᏳᏗᏅ ᏩᏥᎸ! ᎤᎾᏛᏃ ᏩᏥᏍᎫᏛᏂᎸ Julio “ᏞᏍᏗ’Ꭱ ᏲᏥᎯᎮ!” y’know ᎠᎪᎮᎸ ᎠᎵᏍᎩᏍᎬᏭ
segments.translation: There were roadrunners that went by all the time and on the side of the road there were a pile of rocks. He was sitting up there on the rock, the boys were shooting, but they didn’t kill him. They were just shooting nearby him. And he kept moving around. “Hmph!” said Julio. “Let me try it!” Then he threw a rock...and it killed it! It hit it on the head. Then Woodrow said, “We weren’t trying to kill him!” [Julio] was just dancing around.

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.translation: [laughs]

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: They were missing him on purpose.

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.translation: Yeah. “I thought you all were missing because y’all didn’t know how,” he told them.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: [laughs]

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᏚᏚ--ᏥᏚᏓᎴᏤᏛ ᏌᏭ ᏳᏩᎦᏓ...um...ᏙᏅ high school ᎠᎾᏁᏦᏍᎬ ᎠᏯ ᎠᏭ ᏗᏢ Old Gym ᎣᎩᏴᏛ ‘rink-a-dinks’ ᎣᎪᎮᎲ Ꮎ ᎠᏂᏐᎢ...um...”Ꮥ-ᏕᏓᏁᏦᏔᏅᎢ” ᎤᏛᏁ Ꮎ ᏐᎢ coach Mr. Ellis ᏚᏙᎠ...”we’ll play y’all,” ᎤᏛᏅ ᏙᏳ ᏙᏣᏁ--ᎤᏲᎡ ᏃᏨᏁᎸ ᏙᎦᏁᏦᏍᎬ ᎤᏂᎿᎸᏨ Mack Buzzard ᏧᏙᎢᏓ Leon Hill ᏧᏙᎢᏓ Ꮎ ᎠᏰᏟ...uh...Ꭴ--ᏣᏓᎾᎵᏔᏕᎪ ᎥᎾ ᎤᏂᏴᏍᏗ ᏂᎨᎲ ᎤᎾᎵᏍᏓᏴᏗ--ᎤᎾᏟᏍᏗ ᏂᎨᎬᏁᎸ ᎣᏥᏃ ᏂᎬ. Ꮎ ᏍᎩᏃ ᎤᏂᏍᏆᏛᏃ ᏚᏲᏍᏓᏁᎸ Ꮧ-ᏗᏕ-- “ᎩᎶᎨ. ᏄᏓᎴ ᎤᏚᎵᎭ ᏧᏟᏍᏗ?” ᎤᏛᏅ Coach Julio ᎤᏌᎳᏓᏁ ᎤᏬᏰᏂ “ᎦᎪ ᏍᏓᏟᏍᏗ ᏣᏚᎵ Julio?” “ᏂᎯᏅ!” ᏩᎪᎮᎸ ᏗᏕᏲᎲᏍᎩ ᏝᏍᏊ ᎪᎱᏍᏗ ᏳᏛᏁ ᏫᏙᎩᏲᏎ
segments.translation: One time, there was a disagreement. We were in high school they kept us in a room, and they were calling us rink-a-dinks. The coach, his name was Mr. Ellis said we’ll play a game with them. We beat them real bad and they got mad. Mack Buzzard and Leon Hill. Where they jump for the tip off [center court]—they made them get in the circle and fight. And then the coach stopped the fight and asked if anybody else wanted to fight. Julio raised his hand and the coach said, “Who do you want to fight with?” Julio said, “You.” He didn’t say anything, he just turned us loose

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.translation: Mack was always with him.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: Yeah. ᎤᏓᎾᏛ ᏥᎨᎲ Julio...um...ᏓᎵᏆᏛ ᏣᏕᏅ Ꮳ.Ꮣ ᏙᎲ?
segments.translation: He was really nice. You said you were born in Tahlequah, right?

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.translation: Yes.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ...ᏳᏍᏗ ᎠᏎ Ꮳ,Ꮫ.ᎦᏅ ᎨᎮ...uh...ᏣᏚᏓ, ᏣᎵᏏ, ᏗᎨᏣᎦᏴᎵᎨ ᎴᏱᎦ ᏍᏊ ᎠᏂᏃᎮᏢᏍᎬ ᎠᏯ ᎮᏅ ᏥᎩ...um...ᏳᏓᎭ ᏴᏛ.ᎪᏓ ᏂᏗᎦᎵᏍᏙᏗ...uh...”‘ᎸᏢ ᏫᏥᎶᎭ,” Ꮿ--ᎣᎪᎮᎮ ᎠᎨ ᏓᎾᏝᏃᎮ ᎨᏒ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎠᏎᏃ Ꮭ ᎫᏍᏗ ᏱᏣ,Ꮫ.ᎪᏔᏅ ᎫᏍᏗ ᎠᏂᏃᎮᏍᎬ ᏍᎩᎾ...uh...ᏍᎩᏍ ᏱᏍᎩᏃᎯᏏ ᎫᏍᏗ?
segments.translation: I guess you’ve heard your granny, grandpa, or your parents talk about things. But us, they always told us to go away and not be eavesdropping. But you might have heard something they were talking about. Can you tell us something?

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.translation: Like medicine?

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Medicine.

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.translation: They both knew.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: They all knew.

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.text: ᎡᏚᏓ ᎮᏅ...I don’t know why...ᎾᏛᎾ ᏥᎦᏓᏅᏖᎠ,...uh...Ꮩ ᏓᏃᎮᎰ Ꮎ rattlesnake?
segments.translation: I don’t know why – how do you say rattlesnake?

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Uksudi.

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.text: ᏥᏈᏍᏗ--ᎤᎧᏑᏗ ᏥᏈᏍᏗ ᏙᏒᎡ ᏧᎾᏓᎴᏅᏓ ᏓᏁᎲ ᎥᎾ ᏍᎩ ᎦᏁᎩ ᏱᏚᏱᎦ, ᏥᎨᎲ ᎫᏍᏗ ᎮᏅ ᏥᎬ,ᏗᎮ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏥᏕᎧᏅᏫᏍᎬ ᏴᏫ ᎢᎾ ᏓᏳᏂᎶᏒ ᏯᏁᏓ ᏥᎨᎲ...and Granny...Ꭱ..uh...ᏙᏳ ᎠᎩ,ᏍᏗ ᏥᎨᎲ asthma ᏥᎾᏩᎵ,ᏍᏓᏁᎸ...it’s back, but uh...ᏃᏭ ᏣᎦᏔᎲ...I wish I’d listened...ᎠᏎᏃ ᏅᏬᏘ ᎣᏍᏓ ᏥᎾᏮᏁᎴ “ᎯᎢ ᏥᎬᏂ,--ᎣᏍᏓ ᏥᏂᎬᏁᎢ cream ᏓᎦᏑᏴᏂ ᏍᏗᎢᏅᏭ ᎯᎩᏍᎨᏍᏗ ᎢᎦ ᏂᏓᎦᎵᏍᏓᏂᏒ ᎭᏗᏗᏍᎬᎢ,” ᏧᏛᏅ ᏍᎩ ᏂᎦᏛᏁᎲ ᏴᏓ ᏞᏍᏗ Ᏺ’ ᎠᏩᏕᏙ.ᏔᏁᎬ ᎪᎯᏗᏛ ᎢᎤᎷᏨ ᎠᎩᎶᏒᏛ ᎣᏍᏓ ᎣᎰᏪᎮ ᏃᏭᏅ ᎠᏴᎳ...okay...ᎢᎦ ᎮᏅ ᎤᏬᎯᏳ ᎨᎲ Ꮎ ᏦᎳ ᏣᏅᏗ ᏣᎾᏔ Oh gosh.”
segments.translation: Uksudi. He used to look for snake skin and used it for medicine. He said people from long ways off came to get medicine. Still, there are a lot of snakes around there. And Granny, when I was little, I had asthma and granny made medicine for me. I wish I paid attention to what she used. “What I’m fixing here, I’m going to add cream to it. Just eat a little bit every day,” she said. When I was doing that it, it didn’t bother me and then after a long while it came back. It was good and then Ayvl(i), ...okay... he was a true believer of his using tobacco, you know. I thought, “Oh gosh.”

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.text: ᎨᎵᎲ...uh...ᎣᎩᎾᎵᏅ ᎠᎨᏳᏣ Ꮎ Sequoyah ᏙᎩᎾ--ᏦᎩᎾᏙᎵ,Ꮸ Ꮭ ᏯᏩᎾᏔ ᎯᏲᎵᎦ ᏱᎨᎮ Rass Rider? ᎤᏍᏗ Rider’s Cafe ᏥᏄᏮᏅ
segments.translation: I had a friend that went to school at Sequoyah, you might know her, Rass Rider. She had a little Rider’s Cafe.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Yeah, I remember that place.

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.text: ᎥᎾ ᎮᏅ ᏲᏍᏕᏙᎳ Ꮎ ᎠᎨᏳᏣ ᏚᎸᏫ,ᏍᏓᏁᎲ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏍᎪᎯᏭ ᏂᎨᎲᎾ ᏮᏥᎷᎬ ᏩᎩᎧᎲᏍᎬ Ꮎ ᎠᎨᏳᏣ ᎾᏛ ᎠᎴᏅ ᎠᏗᏟᎵᏙᎲ ᏧᏓᏙᎮᎸ ᎾᏛ Granny ᎠᎦᏘᎾᏫᏛᎲ “ᎡᎾᏘᏄᎦ Vian ᏗᏟ,” ᎬᎩ,ᏘᎾᎰᏢ “ᎭᏢ, ᎢᏕᎦ,” ᏥᏲᎮᎸ “ᎩᎶᏛ Smith ᏧᏙᎢᏓ,” ᎠᏬᎮᎲ “ᏙᎲ ᏥᏂᎦᏪᏍᎬ ᏥᎿᏛᏁᎰ?” ᏥᏲᎮᎲ “Ꮻ.ᏁᏓᏭ.” ᏃᏭ ᎥᎾ ᎣᎨᏅᏒ ᏃᏭᏅ ᎤᏛ.ᎯᏍᏗ ᎠᎩ,Ꮫ.ᏛᎲ ᏞᏍᏗ ᏯᏬᎯᏳᏎ ᏍᎩᏳᏍᏗ ᎠᏯ--Ꮓ--Ᏼ ᏦᎦᏕᎶᏆᎥ ᏥᎩ Ꮭ ᎢᎸᎯᏳ ᎠᎦ,Ꮫ.ᎦᏅ ᏱᎨᎮ ᏍᎩᏳᏍᏗ ᏅᏬᏘ ᏥᎩ ᏃᏊᎴ...and uh...ᏝᏍᏊ ᎢᎸᎯᏳ ᎠᏬᎩ,Ꮢ ᏱᎨᎮ...and uh...ᏙᏳᏅ ᎤᏛ.ᎯᏍᏗ ᎠᎩ,Ꮫ.ᏛᎮᏢᏍᎬ ᎤᏠᏱᏭ ᏥᎾᎩᏪᎮᎸ ᏥᏃᏎᎸ
segments.translation: I used to be there cause the girl worked there. I would go home about 10 o’clock, she would drop me off and they said she started running around. And when she takes Granny with her, “Let’s take her to Vian.” “Where are we going?” I said. “To somebody named Smith,” she said. “Why do you do what he says to do?” “Let’s just go over there,” she said. So we went, and this old man was asking me. I said I didn’t believe in this stuff. I had never heard of it being medicine, I had never used tobacco and I never smoked. But this old man was asking questions and he was saying the same thing.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: [laughs]

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.text: “ᏥᎬᏲᎮ ᎮᏅ” ᎠᎪᎮᎴᏛ ᎡᎵᏏ...and uh...Ꮭ ᎫᏍᏗ ᏱᎦᏗᎮ Pall Mall ᏕᎦᏂᏛ ᏕᎦᎵᏗᏍᏛ ᏂᏚᏮᏅ ᎡᏠᎩ ᏍᎩᎾ Ꮭ ᏯᏩᎾᏔ ᏂᏚᏮᏁᎸ Ꮎ ᎤᏛ.ᏍᎯᏗ upside down...ᏧᏍᏗᎩᏐᏅ ᏚᏩᏃᏢ ᎠᏥᏃᏎᎸ ᎪᎩ,ᏒᏅ...uh east Ꮩ ᏚᏙᎠ east ᎯᎢᏅ ᏗᏢ ᎠᏓ...all directions...ᎪᎩ,ᏍᎨᏍᏗ ᎠᏦᏔᏍᎨᏍᏗ “ᎮᏍᏗᏅ ᎦᎵᏦᏕ ᏱᏥᏴᏔᏅ,” ᏙᏅ chicken house ᏄᏮᏁ ᎡᎵᏏ...ᎥᎾ ᏚᏂᏢᏛ ᎪᎯᏗᏛ a week, two weeks-Ꮲ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎾᏩᏛᏁᎸ ᎠᎩ,ᏓᎦ,ᏍᎬ ᏒᎾᎴ ᎦᏗᏗᏍᎬ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎦᏛᏁᎲ ᎠᎬᏱ ᎮᏅ “Phew!” ᎦᏗᎥᏭ Ꮭ--ᏃᏭᏛ ᎪᎯᏴ ᎠᏩᎴᏅᏭ ᏩᎩᎾᏌᏁᏌ And uh...boy about 3rd week-‘ᏛᏃ ᎦᎢᏒ stump Ꮵ--ᎥᎾᏛ ᏩᏬᏢ Ꮎ ᏂᎦᎦᏔᎲᏍᎬ ᎠᎩ,ᏑᎵᎪᏨ
segments.translation: “I told you,” Granny said to him. I wasn’t saying anything and my aunt brought packs of Pall Mall cigarettes. I don’t know what the old man did with them but they were opened upside down when he brought them back. So, he told my aunt how I should smoke them, first the east –what's the name for ‘east?’-- smoke and blow in all [four] directions. He said, “Do not bring them in the house.” My aunt had a chicken house and that’s where she put them. I did that every day when I got up and I was sure getting tired of it after a while. At first, I just puffed a little bit and then later I went to really smoking it. And uh...boy about going on the 3rd week, I was sitting on the stump and I quit turning around.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: [laughs]

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: [laughs] So you just become a smoker?

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.text: ᏃᏭ ᏥᎪᎩᏍᎬᏭ and uh...Granny ᏥᏃᏎᎸ “ᏂᎯᏛᏃ ᎭᎴᏂ ᎠᏩᏚᎵ ᎠᏬᎩ,ᏍᏗ,” ᏥᏲᎮᎸ “ohh,” she said. ᎪᎯᏗ ᎮᏅ ‘Ᏺ ᏚᏩᏒ ᎪᎩ,ᏍᏗ ᏃᏊᎴ ᏨᎩ.ᎾᏮᏅ ᏭᎴᏅ ᏣᎩ,ᏑᎵᎪᏨ. “ᎮᏍᏗᏅ ᎢᎸᎯᏳ ᏥᎰᎩ,Ꮜ ᏃᏭ ᏁᎳᎩ ᎨᎮᏍᏗ, ᎯᎾ ᎣᏍᏗ ᏂᎬᏴᏁᎸ, ᏃᏭ ᏧᏓᎴᏅᏓ ᎤᏓᏂᎸ,” ᎪᎯᏗ ᏥᎶᎯ ᏣᏩᎴᏅᎲᎮ about George-Ꮥ ᏧᏲᎱᏒ I was probably about 38 ‘Ꮲ ᏣᏬᎩ,Ꮢ ᎾᎯᏳ ᏧᎴᏅᎲ And uh...but I don’t know...ᎤᏬᎵᏗᏛ ᎨᎲ ᏝᏙ ‘Ᏺ ᎰᏩ ᏯᎩᏰᎸ ᏍᎩᎾ I mean...ᏝᏴ ᎣᎦᏛ.Ꮢ ᏱᎩ “ᎦᏛ.--Ꮭ ᎠᎦ,Ꮫ.ᎦᏅ ᏱᎨᎮ ᏍᎩᏳᏍᏗ ᎫᏍᏗ,” ᎦᏥᏲᎮᎲ ᏍᎩᏭ ᎮᏅ ᏳᏍᏗ
segments.translation: I was just smoking. And I told Granny, “You got me started, now I need to smoke all the time.” “Oh,” she said, but she bought the cigarettes for a while and then she cured me and I quit. “Don’t ever start smoking again,” she said. I didn’t smoke a long time, but when George died, I started smoking again and it’s funny because I went back to smoking then, but I don’t feel good about it. And I guess I’m not grown up because I have never heard anything like this before.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Somebody was here a while ago and they were talking about ghosts.

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.translation: [laughs]

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᏱᎦᏥᏍᎦᏍᏓᏌ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎠᏂᎨᏳᏣ ᎫᏍᏗ ᎠᎦ,Ꮫ.ᎦᏅ ᎠᏂᏃᎮᏍᎬ Ᏺ’ : Like...ᏄᎾᎵᏍᏓᏁᎲ ᎡᎵᏏ ᎮᏅ ᏱᎧᏃᎲᎳ ᎠᏎᏛ ᎦᏚ ᏯᏂᏝᎲᎦ ᏥᎨᎲ table-Ꭲ Ꭹ--ᎫᏍᏗ ᏳᎾᏕᏙ.Ꮧ “ᏙᏭ ᏍᎩ ᏣᏅᏁ ᎩᎶ ᏯᏴᏟᎯ ᏃᏊᎴ ᎫᏍᏗ ᏱᏣᏕᏙ.Ꮧ ᎤᏲᏏᎰ, ᎮᏅ” ᏣᏬᎮᎸ “ah,” and uh...ᏃᏊᎴ ᏯᎩᏅᏨ ᎨᎲ pine Ꮎ cedar, I think it’s cedar...ᎠᎪᎲᏍᏔᏅ ᎦᎵᏦᏕ...and stuff like that, but...ᎠᏂᎨᏳᏣ ᏱᎬᎩ,ᏒᏎᎵ ᎦᏥᏍᎦᏍᏓᏁᎲ ᎦᏥᏃᏎᎲ ᎫᏍᏗ ᎬᎩᏃᏎᎲ ᎠᏎᏅ Ꮭ ᎢᎸᎯᏳ ᎪᎱᏍᏗ ᎠᎩᎪᎲ ᏱᎩ ᎠᏯ “ᎪᎱᏍᏗ’Ꭱ ᎠᎩ,ᏒᏂ!” ᏯᎾᏗᏛ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎪᎯᏴ ...it was crazy though.
segments.translation: I would scare the girls when I told them I heard something like that. my Granny would tell stories and they would put a biscuit on the table if something was bothering them. I asked why the biscuit? And Granny said, “If something is coming in, or if something is bothering you, they are just hungry,” she told me. -- “Ah.” And then, when I laid down. Pine, Cedar; I think it was cedar. She would burn cedar through the house. ...stuff like that... But, when the girls came to see me, I would scare them. But I would tell them I had never seen anything, but the girls they always said, “Something’s touching me.” It was crazy though.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Let me tell…you didn’t know Rattler?

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.translation: Rattler.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Rattler Julio he was called.

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.text: I don’t know but...ᏙᏳ ᎮᏅ ᎠᎦ,Ꮫ.ᎦᏅ ‘Ꭱ
segments.translation: I don’t know but I have heard the name before.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᎮᏍᏗᎡ ᎡᏚᏥ ᏱᎨᎮ ᏙᏳ ᎨᎲ ᎠᏎᏃ “ᎡᏚᏥ,” ᏃᏦᎮᎮ ᎨᎲ ᎣᎩᏚᏥ ᎣᏥᏰᎸ ᎨᎲ ᎾᎾ ᏝᏅ ᏱᏔᏅᏓᏗ ᎠᏂ-Sam?
segments.translation: He wasn’t my uncle, but we called him that. He was an uncle to us. How about the Sam’s?

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.translation: The Sam’s?

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Mary, yeah…and Ron.

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.translation: Little Joe.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᏌᏭ ᏳᏩᎦᏛ...uh...ᎡᏠᎩ ᎤᏂᏓᏒᏎᎴ Ꮎ....uh...ᎧᏅᏧᏪ ᏚᏙᎥ Ꮎ Rattler ᎧᏅᏧᏪ ᏧᎾᏓᏝᏫᏍᏓ ᎾᎾ ‘Ꮲ ᏯᏖᏃ ᎤᏂᏰᏍᏛᏁᎴ ᎧᏅᏥᏭ ᎾᏅ...uh...Mary, John ᎤᏍᏓᏴᎲᏍᎩ ᎥᎾ ᎤᎾᏂᏏᏁᏅ ᎧᏅᏥ ᏭᏂᏏᏂᏗ ‘ᏢᏅᏃ ᏒᏃᏱ ᎨᏒ ᎫᏍᏗ ᎤᏕᏙ.ᏔᏁ ᏍᎩᎾ...uh...Mary “Ahh! ᎫᏍᏗ ᎠᏩᏕᏙ.Ꮧ!” ᏧᏛᏅ ᎮᏅ
segments.translation: One time, they spent the night with my aunt. The one named Kanvtsuwe and Rattler. Kanvtsuwe he was living with them. They put covers down on the floor for them to sleep on. Mary laid down with John on Kanvtsuwe’s spot and sometime during the night something bothered her and she yelled, “Ahhh, something’s bothering me!”

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.translation: [laughs]

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: “ᎠᏯ ᏱᎬᏪᎵᏎ” ᎡᎵᏍᎨ--ᎤᏪᎵᏎ ᎧᏅᏥᏭ ᏥᎨᎲ “Haw! ᏪᏌ ᎤᏩᏏ!”
segments.translation: “They’re going to think it’s me,” Kanvtsi thought. Then he said, “It’s just that cat!”

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: [laughter]

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᎤᏬᎵᏗᎮ ᎤᏛ.ᎯᏍᏗ ᏥᎨᎲ...um...Ꮩ ᎤᏍᏗ ᎢᏣᏛᏁᎮ ᎢᏣᎵᏍᏕᎵᏙᏗ ᎢᎩ--Ꭲ--ᏃᏭ--ᏃᏭ Ꮴ-ᏤᏅᏒ ᎨᏒ ᎢᏣᎷᏣ ᎨᏒᏃ
segments.translation: Yeah, he was a funny man. What did you all do to live when you came home? Yeah, he was a funny man. What did you all do to live when you came home?

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.translation: For money?

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Money, or whatever.

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.text: Uh...ᏦᏣᎵᏍᏕᎵᎮ ᎧᏅᏥ ᎪᏢᏍᎬ ᏃᏊᎴ ᏒᎩ ᎣᎩᏲᎲ ᎦᎾᏕᎬ...and uh, what was the other? Ꭺ.ᏧᎾ ᏧᏓᎴᏅᏓᏭ ᏣᏪᏲᎲᏍᎬ Ᏺ’...and she even taught me, Ꮩ ᏣᏃᎮᎰ Ꮎ ᎢᏡᎬ red bud? ᏣᏪᏲᏅ ᏣᎩ,ᏍᏗᎬ. and, toothbrush Ꮭ ᎢᎸᎯᏳ ᎠᏮ--ᏥᏂ--ᏯᏮᏰ’Ꮥ...and uh...”Ꭿ’Ꭱ ᏂᏨᏁᏗ” ᏧᏛᏅ Ꮎ root ᏚᎶᏒ ᏯᎬᎭᎳ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎯᎢᏛ ‘Ꮲ ᏯᏓᎵᏍᏆᎳ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏥᏕᎦᏅᎦᎳᏛ ᏍᎩᏭ ᎣᏨ,ᏗᎲ toothbrush juice-ᎢᏅ boy ᎣᏍᏓ ᏥᎨᎲ...from that root. And ᏍᎩᏭ ᎬᏗᎲ...ᎣᏍᏓ
segments.translation: We were helping to make kanvtsi and we looked for wild onion, that she sold. And Kotsuna and whatever else. She was teaching me. She even taught me… what do they call that red bud? She taught me when I was little. I never did own a toothbrush. She would clean them, she would cut them and then we would clean the roots with a toothbrush and juice to clean our teeth. That root that’s what we used. They were so good.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᏝᏍ ᏂᎪᎯᎸ ᏳᏅᏍᎦᎶᏕᎨ ᏍᎩᎾ (...) ᏍᎩ ᏥᎾᏛᏁᎮ...Ꮭ ᏯᏩᎾᏔ Ꮹ-Ꮹ-ᏫᏓᎩᏍᎬ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏂᎪᎯᎸ ᎮᏅ Ꮷ-Ꮷ-ᏧᏅᏍᎦᎶᏕᎪ ᎨᎲ ᏦᎰ ᏥᎬᏫᏍᏓ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏧᏅᏍᎦᏢᏅ ᎨᎲ
segments.translation: He didn’t always have it in his mouth? (...) used to do that. I don’t know, but he went and got it somewhere. He would always have that in his mouth. He looked like a cottonmouth, with those in his mouth all the time.

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.translation: You have never chewed it before?

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: Huh uh, ᎮᏍᏗ, ᎢᎸᎯᏳ ᎠᎩᏍᏙᏓ, ᏱᎩ,
segments.translation: No, I never chewed it.

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.text: Ꭳ Ᏺ’ ᎢᎦ ᎣᏍᏓ ᏥᎨᎮ Ꮎ...how you—Ꮎ toothpaste ᏥᏄᏍᏗ ᏍᎩᏭ ᏧᏍᏗ Ꮎ ᏄᏍᏛ Ꮎ root ᎣᏍᏓ ᏥᎨᎲ Ꭼ.ᏙᏗ Ꮎ ᏣᎾᏅᏍᎦᏢᏍᎬ ᏂᎪᎯᎸ ᏍᎩ ᏥᎬ,ᏗᎲ ᎡᎵᏏ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏏᏅ ᏂᎦᏓ ᏥᏕᎦᏂᏙᎬ ᏧᏲᎱᏒ
segments.translation: It was really good. It tasted just like toothpaste, the root, the people that used tobacco that’s what they used to clean their teeth. He still had all of his teeth when he died.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᎾᏍ Garrett ᏥᏓᏃᎮᏍᎬ ᏍᎩᏍ ᏳᏍᏗ ᎠᏅᏍᎦᏢᏍᎨ?
segments.translation: Oh, you mean that what they call Garrett?

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.translation: [laughs] Strong.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Did you ever try it?

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.text: Huh uh. ᎤᏴᏍᏛ ᏣᏩᎵᏒᏍᏔᏅᎾ ᎤᎾᏛ ᎫᏍᏗ ᎾᏩᎵᏍᏓᏁᎸ ᏥᏴᏐᎵ ᏭᏴᏢ
segments.translation: Huh uh. It had a strong taste. I just smelled it and something almost happened to me when it went in my nose.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᎾᏛ ᎡᏥ ᎤᎸᏉᏛ ᏥᎨᎲ Ᏺ’ ᎤᏅᏍᎦᏢᏗ
segments.translation: And my mother she really liked it.

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.translation: [laughs] Days Working.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: Ꮭ Ᏺ’ ᏍᎩᏳᏍᏗ ᏙᏳ ᎮᏅ ᎾᏛ...snuff ᏣᏃᎮᎲ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏍᎩᎾ and...ᏂᎪᎯᎸᏛ ᏧᎰ ᏥᎨᎲ...um...ᎦᏳᏅᏍᎦᏢᎾ ᏍᏊ ᏱᏕᎧᏃᎦ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏳᏓᎭᏛ ᏥᏂ,ᏧᏍᏙ ᎤᎵᏥᏈᏗ ᎨᏒ ᏃᏭ ᎣᏣᏕᎰᏍᎬᏅ ᎯᎢᎡ ᏃᎦᏛᏃ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏗᎦᏅᎦᎸᎯ’ᏅᎡ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎠᎢᏒ ᏱᏕᎧᏃᎦ, ᏥᎨᎲ ᎤᎸᏉᏙ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏂᎪᎯᎸ ᏧᏅᏍᎦᏠ ᏥᎨᎲ
segments.translation: Not that. The ‘snuff’ they called it. She always had it, and she sang with it in her mouth. Sometimes she had her spit can and she would spit and clean her mouth and keep on singing. She really liked it and had it in her mouth all the time.

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.text: ᏧᏂᎳᏫᏍᏗᏅ ᏃᏭ ᏂᎪᎯᎸ ᎣᏤᏙᎰ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏧᎾᏛᏅ
segments.translation: They said we were at all the time.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Where were y’all?

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Cherry Tree.

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.text: ᎡᏙᏓ ᏤᎲ Salem-Ꭲ ᏥᏙᎩᏘᏅᎲ ᎦᏅᏓᏗᏍᎪ ᏍᏊ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏃᏊᎴ ᏧᏲᎱᏒᏃ Mama ᎩᏔᏲ ᏦᏤ-ᏦᏤᏙᎲ Mama-Ꮓ ᏧᏑᎵᎪᏨ Granny ᏥᏙᎩᏘᏁᎬ and-Ꮓ ᎬᏃ ᏥᏭᎴᏅᎲ...but uh...ᎣᏍᏓ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏗᎦᏛ.ᎪᏗ I look around...ᏳᏓᎭ ᏧᏂᎳᏫᏍᏗ ᏗᏂᏲᏟ “Haw, ᎠᏯ Ꮭ ᏍᎩ ᏱᎬᏩᏛᏁᏗ ᏱᎨᎮ,” y’know ᏴᎯᎪᏩᏔ stage-ᎢᏛ ᏯᎾᏢᏍᏓ ᏳᏓᎭ ᏳᏩ---[unclear] And uh...”ᏱᏣᏚᎵ ᎮᎾ...,” ᎦᏥᏲᎮᎰ “ᎾᎥ ᎮᎾ ᎤᎵᏍᏛᏡᏍᏗ ᏱᎨᎮ Ᏺ’ ᏍᎩ ᏱᏕᏂᎬᎦ church-Ꭲ if they don’t go...Ꮎ ᏗᏂᏲᏟ ᏓᏂᎳᏫᎬ ᏄᏁᏅᏗ ᏱᎩ ᎠᎭᏂᏛ ᎯᏯᎡᏍᏗ ᏔᎵᏍᏛᏡᏂ ᏙᏥ--ᏔᏛ.ᏓᏍᏔᏂ,” ᎦᏥᏲᎮᎸ ᏙᏳ ᏙᎯ ᏄᎾᏛᏁᎸ
segments.translation: Cherry Tree. When my dad was alive, he took us to Salem Church; I remember that. When he died and mama took us to Cherry Tree. When mama quit taking us there then granny took us, then Ganotsi started. But it was good to hear it well. I think back sometimes with how the kids are today I couldn’t have done that. I see kids running around the stage nowadays. “If you want to...” I tell them. “We could have someone sit nearby in the church, that’s what (...) would do to them. If they don’t go... The kids who don’t go to service.” -- “You will be in here, you’re going to sit down and you’re going to listen,” I told them. They really did calm down.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Well they have to learn, ain’t it? While they’re there.

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.translation: He is talking about something important, I tell them.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Can you sing in Cherokee?

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.translation: Yeah. Yep.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᎾᎾ Gina ᏕᎧᏃᎩᏍᎩᏍ ᏥᏯᏛ.ᎦᏅ ᎨᎵ Gina ᏝᎨ.?
segments.translation: How about Gina, can she sing? I think I’ve heard her before.

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.text: ᏱᎧᏃᎦ’Ꭱ Ꮭ ᏍᎩ ᎢᎦ ᏳᏃᎩᏐ ᏗᏂᏲᏟ ᎮᏅ ᏱᏕᎨᏲᎲᎦ ᏳᏓᎭ ᏧᎾᏕᎶᏆᏍᏗ Ꮭ ᏯᏩᎾᏔ ᏳᏍᏗ ᎤᏂᏃᎩᏒ ᏌᏊ ᏳᏩᎦᏓ gym-Ꭲ ᏧᎾ--ᏥᏚᎾ--ᏍᎩ ᏥᏄᎾᏛᏁᎸ ᏃᏊᎴ ᏣᎳᎩᎭ ᏚᏪᏲᏅ...what is it...Ꮎ flag
segments.translation: Yeah, she can sing. But she don’t sing that much. She can teach children though, at the school. I can’t remember what they sang. One time, they were singing in the gym, then she taught them to -- What’s it called? The flag?

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: Oh! Ꮎ Pledge of Allegiance ᎠᏃᎮ?
segments.translation: The Pledge of Allegiance, they say?

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.translation: Yes.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: She taught them that?

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.text: Uh huh. And something else, too...ᎠᏎᏃ Ᏺ’ ᏙᏳ, ᎤᏬᏚᎯ ᎾᏂᏪᏍᎪ “Ꭲ-ᎢᎦᏓ ᎮᏅ ᏙᏳ ᎤᎾᏚᎵ ᎤᎾᏕᎶᏆᏍᏗ,” ᏣᏗᎲ ᏃᏭᏅ ᎢᎦᏓ ᎠᎭᏂ ᏃᏊᎴ ᎤᏍᎦᏃᎵ ᎤᏬᎵᏗᏅ she said...ᎠᏩᏚᎵᎰ ᎮᏅ ᎫᏍᏗ...to keep them, uh...’ᏙᏛ ᏴᏓ? ᎤᎾᏚᎵᏍᎩ ᏳᎵᏍᏙᏗ...and she makes everything fun for them, and...ᏕᎨᏲᎲᏍᎬ
segments.translation: Yeah, they really sound pretty. Some of them really want to learn. But some are real slow. They need somebody to work with them to make them want to learn. She makes everything fun for them when she’s teaching.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: When you all came back to Cherry Tree did you all have electricity?

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.text: Huh uh! How old was I? I was...almost 19 before we got...uh...electric ᎠᎻᏅ...ᎠᎻ’Ꮥ Ꮭ Electric-ᎢᏭᎢᎦ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎪᎯᏗ ᎠᎻᏅ Ꮟ ᏥᏙᏥᎫ.ᎩᏍᎬ ᎾᏅ sink ᏥᏅᎬᏁᎸ ᎦᎵᏦᏕ kitchen-Ꭲ “ᎡᎵᏍᏛ ᎠᎻ ᎨᎯᏔᏲᎯ ᎣᏍᏓ ᏳᏅᏂᏗ sink ᏧᎾᏨᏅ ᎫᏍᏗ ᏄᏓᎴ ᏫᏣᏢᎦ,” ᏥᏲᎮᎲ but uh....ᎠᏯᏛ ᎦᏗᏟᏙᎲᏃ ᎠᎩᏅᏒ ᎠᏎᏃ ᎠᎹ well ᏧᏂᏍᏆᎵᏒ
segments.translation: Huh uh. How old was I? I was almost 19 when we got electric [unclear]. Back then there was all electricity, but we still had to draw our water, but they put a sink in the kitchen. “You could ask somebody to put water in for you. Since you got a sink, you just got something else in it,” I told her. But I was the one that did the running around to do the talking and get something done. They dug a well.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: They hook it up to the house?

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.text: “ᏃᏭᏛ ᎢᏣᏓᏄᎸᏅ ᏂᏓᎦᎵᏍᏔᏂ!” ᏣᏬᎮᎸ ...cause... ᎠᎻᏅ woodstove-ᎢᏅ ᏍᏊ ᎤᏍᏗ ᏧᎲ ...cause... ᎡᎵᏏ ...she was like... 4’9 ᎤᏍᏗᏭ ᎮᎾ ᏥᎨᎲ...and uh...ᎥᎾ ᏲᏍᏗᏙ.Ꮣ ᏱᏥᏙ.Ꮣ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎠᏯ ᏱᎩ ᎤᏗᏞᎦ ᏱᏫᏂᎦᎵᏍᏓ ᏃᏭᏅ table-Ꭲ ᏱᏫᏥᏝᎲᎦ ᏱᏕᎬᏗᏯ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏃᏊᎴ ᏔᎵᏃ ᏕᎬ,Ꮭ ᏃᏭ rinse ᏕᎬᏁᎲ LouiseᏃ Ꮎ ᏥᏥᎦᏎᏍᏗ ᏗᎩ.ᏲᏗᏍᎩ ᎤᏬᎵᏗᎲ ᎠᏎᏃ Ꮭ ᏍᏓᏱ ᏱᎨᎮ y’know? Boy, GrannyᏛ Ᏺ’ muscles ᏂᏚᏮᏅ ᏗᎦᏅᏍᎨᏂ, arms, and she was 82 ᎨᎵ ᏧᏲᎱᏒ ᎤᏍᎦᎮᏗ ᎤᏝᏂᎩᏓ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎾᏃ arthritis ᎩᎳ ᎾᎯᏳᏛ ᎩᎳ ᏧᎴᏅᎲ “ᏳᏓᎭ ᏓᏪᏍᏓᏁᎲ ᎠᎭᏂᏴ,” ᏯᏓ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎠᏯᏅ ᏗᎩᏲᎤᏟᏃ ᎾᎥ hips going out.
segments.translation: “Now everybody’s going to get lazy!” she told me. She had water and a little cook stove. Granny was little, she 4’9. I would put water in a big pan and put it on top of the stove and when it got real hot, I put it on the table and washed the dishes. I would put them on the table and Louise was, the one I was taking care of, was drying the dishes. She wasn’t really bad off and Granny she really had them muscles. Her legs, arms, I think she was 82 when she died. She was strong, until she got the arthritis. That’s when she started hurting. “It’s hurting my arms,” she would say. And me, I’m getting crippled too, my hips are going out.

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.translation: [laughs]

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Were y’all making a garden?

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.text: Mhmm! ᏂᎪ’Ꮈ...uh...ᎦᏁᎵ,ᏗᎰ’Ꭱ ᎦᏥᎨ--I mean--ᎦᏥᏰᏲᎲᏍᎪ ᏗᏂᏲᏟ ᏙᏳ, ᎤᏍᏗᏭ ᎠᏎᏃ ᎯᎾ ᏣᏓᎴᏂᏃ ᏙᏓᏲ--ᏥᏈᏯᏛ ᏚᏂᎾᏝ ᎫᏍᏗ...like ᎩᏟ Ꮭ ᏯᏩᎾᏔ ᏦᎢ ᎢᏯᏂ Chihuahua ᏌᏭᏅ pitbull ᏌᏭᏅ Ꮎ ᏗᎦᎳᏯᏅᎯᏓ ‘ᏙᏛ ᏣᏃᎮᎰ? ᏥᏳᎪᏗ ᏗᎦᏙᎦ
segments.translation: Mmhm, all the time. Sometimes I try to teach them how to make a garden, but it’s just a little place. But now it’s beginning to—they just got too many dogs. I think they have three Chihuahuas, one pitbull, and one with long legs, what is it called?

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: It’s not a greyhound, is it?

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.translation: No, it’s Doberman.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Doberman, oh!

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.translation: And uh...2 pot belly pigs

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: [laughs]

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.text: And uh....ᎠᏄᏕ...ᎠᏎ ᎠᎾᏨᏏᏰᏍᎪ ᏥᏔᎦ ᎡᎰ Chinese I guess I don’t know Ꮎ ᏗᏂᏅᏍᎨᏂ ᏌᏭ Game Rooster ᏌᏭ “ᎢᏥᏑᎵᎪᎯᏍᏗ ᏥᏂᏣᏛᏁᎠ,” ᎦᏥᏲᎮᎰ “Pin them pigs up, Ꮭ ᎮᏅ Ᏺ’ ᏂᎬ. ᏥᎾᎾᏛᏁ you can’t grow nothing.”
segments.translation: There’s also a chicken. One they call ‘Chinese’. It’s got furry legs. And one is a Game Rooster. I told them, “Y’all gonna have to quit doing this. You have to pen your pigs up. They roaming around and you can’t grow nothing.”

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᏝᏍ Ᏺ’ ᏗᏥᎯᏍᏗ ᏱᏗᏥᎾᏝᎡ ᏏᏆ Ᏺ’?
segments.translation: Did you all have the pigs to kill?

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.translation: Yes.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Could you talk about that?

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.text: ᎠᏯᏲᏛ Ᏺ ᎤᏩᏌ ᏌᏭ ᏯᏥᏴᏛ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎣᏍᏓᏅ ᏣᏁᏠᎲ Ꮭ ᏂᎦᎵᏍᏗᎲᏭ I think August 2ndᏛ ᏳᎵᏍᏔᏁᏏ ᏥᏈᏍᏙᏒᏅ ᏯᏂᎷᎦ Ꮎ ‘ᏚᏚ ᎤᏕᏘᏱᏍᎬ
segments.translation: Mhmm. They would put one up in a pin and fed it real good. They didn’t feed it just anything, so around 2 August, a whole bunch of people came for grandpa’s birthday.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Ohhh, that’s what the hog meat was for.

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.translation: Then they gave some meat to everyone as they went home.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᏏᏓᏁᎳᏍ ᎾᎥ ᏂᏣᏛᏁ like your uncles aunts ᏍᎩᏳᏍᏗ?
segments.translation: Were all your family close by each other? Like your aunts and uncles?

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Were they nearby? Did they live close by?

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.translation: Mhmm. All but, Gadeti.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᏳᏛ...ᏍᎨ....ᏍᎩᎧᎾ ᏍᎩᎧᎾ Ft. Gibson ᏥᎦᏁᎸ Ᏻ-ᏳᏓᎭᏭ ᏥᏙᏍᏓᏓᎪᏩᏛ.ᏔᏂᏙ Ᏺ’ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎾᎯᏳ ᏥᏓᎩᎸᏫᏍᏓᏁᎲ Ꮎ Cherokee Nation
segments.translation: That’s the one that lived in Ft. Gibson. I used to see her every once in a while when I worked at the Cherokee Nation.

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.text: Boy ᎠᎬᏱᏕ I guess Ꮎ ᎠᎨᏳᏣ ᎾᎥ maybe in her ᏔᎵᏍᎪᎯ’Ꮲ ᎠᎯᎵᏒ ᎤᏁᎫᏥᏛ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏍᎩᎾ Thomas ᎮᏅ ᏥᏃᏎᎲ ‘Ꮲ ᎢᎾ ᏫᏣᏓᏰᎶᏒ “Huh uh,” ᎠᏗᎲ ‘ᏚᏚ ᎮᏅ ᏌᏭ ᏳᏩᎦᏓ ᎠᏗᏔᏍᎩ ᎮᏅ ᏥᎨᎲ Ᏺ’ ᏍᎩᎾ Ꮎ ᎠᏂᏁᎳ ᎤᏁᎫᏥᏓ ᏣᎾᏁᎵᏗᎲ ᎤᎾᏓᎢᏅᏙᏗ ᎡᏚᏓ ... ᎠᏓᏁᎸ ᏭᏂᎷᏨ Julio ᏤᏙᎲ ᏌᏭ ᏳᏩᎦᏓ ᏧᏓᎾᏫᏍᏔᏅ ᎦᏄᎳ ᎠᎦᎵᏍᎬ ᏍᎩᏭ ᏥᏭᏅ--ᏣᏥᏁᏒ ᎡᏚᏓ Ᏼ--ᏴᏥᏮᏥᎧᏅ ᏥᏓᏰᎪᏐᎮᎸ “ᏙᎨ. ᎤᎵᏍᏓᏁᎴ?” ᎡᎵᎮ ᏕᏍᏗᏢᏍᎬ.
segments.translation: Boy, but first, that girl, she was about in her 20s and she was a character. I was telling Thomas, “That’s where you get your silliness too.” “Huh-uh,” he said. One time, grandpa, he used to drink all the time. And the ones that were living with him they were trying to run him down. Julio was there one time. He took off while mowing the yard, he picked up grandpa laying there and put him somewhere. Grandpa jumped all over him. “What’s wrong with him anyway?” he probably thought. You two are sleepy?

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.translation: [laughs]

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: That's right.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᏍᎩᏛ ᎾᏩᎵᏍᏓᏁᎲ ᏦᎢ ᏳᏩᎦᏓ ᏗᎧᏚ.ᎴᏂ ᏩᏬᎰᎾᏔᏅ ditch-Ꭲ. ᏥᎸᏍᎬ ᏥᎯᎵᏒ ᏙᏳᏅ ᏣᏃᏎ ᎪᎱᏍᏗ’Ꭱ “ᎯᎢ” ᏥᎾᏅᏁ ᏍᎩ ᎮᏅ ᏗᏮᏂᏗ
segments.translation: Same thing happened to me. I drove three cars into a ditch. I was sleepy while I was driving. What do they call it? That thing that goes like “this?” I had to have it on.

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.translation: At night?

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.translation: Is it CPAP?

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.translation: CPAP.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: That’s what I had to have on.

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.translation: Do you use one?

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᎠᎩᏄᎸᎲᏍᎪ Ꮵ--ᎯᎠ ᏄᏍᏛ ᏥᎦᏅᎪᎬ ᎤᏃᎴ ᏌᏭ ᏳᏩᎦᏓ ᏣᎩᏄᎸᏅ ᎣᏍᏓ ᏳᎵᏍᏙᏗ
segments.translation: I couldn’t use it, that air was coming out on the sides. It didn’t work for me.

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.translation: I would’ve been afraid too.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᏥᏓᏩᏓᏲᏒᏭ ᎮᏍᏗᏅ ᏄᏓᎴ ᎤᏂᎾᎡ ᎡᎷᏭ ᏓᏤᏢ ᏯᏂᎾ ᏃᏭᏥᎩ ᏩᎩᎦᏛᏅ ᎠᏎ ᏩᎩᎦᏛᏅ ᏱᎩ
segments.translation: Yeah, I just gave up. I guess that was the first thing they had. They probably have better ones now. I need to go check on it.

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.translation: Gina uses one.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Is it good?

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.text: I don’t know. ᎮᏍᏗ ᎰᏩ ᏳᏔᏃ ᏳᏓᎭᏭ man, [gasps] ᏯᏓᏛ ᏱᏨᏂᏱ ᏣᏗᎮ “Ꮭ ᏱᏥᎸᏉᏗᎰ,” ᏧᏛᏅ ᎯᏛ ᏄᏍᏛ ᎩᎦᎭ ᏓᏳᏛᎴᏂ
segments.translation: I don’t know. She hardly uses it. Sometimes it felt like it’s choking me. Her face was real red. She didn’t like it.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Yes, yes.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Some people when they talk about it, they make it sound like it’s a good thing.

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.text: ᎣᏍᏓ, phew. I gotta go for that.
segments.translation: Good. I gotta go for that.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: Um...’Ꮩ ᎤᏍᏗ ᏱᎦᏛᏁᏗ Ꮿ.Ꮣ ᏥᎩᏲᎱᏒ ᏣᎳᎩ ᎢᎩᏲᎱᏎᏗ ᏂᎨᎲᎾ ‘Ꮩ ᎤᏍᏗ ᏱᎦᏛᏁᎳ Ꮿ.Ꮣ?
segments.translation: What do you think we should do about losing our language? Just so we don’t lose it, what should we do?

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.text: ᏂᎦᏓ ᏓᏳᎾᏕᎳᎰᏏ ᎤᏂᏬᏂᎯᏍᏗᏭ ᏧᏁᏅᏒ ᏂᎪ’Ꮈ ᏍᏊ ᎾᏃᎵᎬᎾ ᏱᎩ ᏗᏂᏲᏟ ᎠᎭᏂ ᏥᎾᎾᏛᏁ ᏂᎪ’Ꮈ ᏱᏓᏝᏃᎮ ᏩᏃᎵᏥᎦ ᎮᏅ ᎠᏓᏁᎸ ᏍᎩ ᎾᎾᏛᏁ Ꮭ ᏙᏳ, ᎣᏍᏓ ᏱᎦᏥᎵ--ᏱᎪᎵᎪ ᎾᏂᏪᏍᎬ ᎠᏎᏃ ᏯᏆ,Ꮫ.ᏍᏔᏅ you--ᎦᏛ.Ꭹ Ꮎ ᎤᏍᏗ Ᏺ-ᎣᎦ-ᎣᏍᏓᏛ.ᎯᏍᏔᏅᏅ ᏗᏲᎤᏟ ᏂᎪ’Ꮈ ᏣᎳᎩ ᎣᏍᏗᏬᏂᏍᎬ ᎤᏛ.Ꮢ ᏦᎢᏛ‘ᎮᏢ ᏳᏕᏘᏴᏓ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎤᎴᏅᎲ ᎦᏬᏂᏍᎬ “Ꮒ!” ᏧᏛᏅ ᏧᏂᎳᏫᏍᏗ ᏬᏥᎦ,Ꮫ. “ᎠᎨ ᏩᎧ!” ᏧᏛᏅ “What’d she say? What’d she say?” Ꮎ ᎠᏂᏐᎢ ᏓᎾᏓᎳᎢᏴ...and I said, uh...”ᎢᏣᏎᎮ Ꮎ ᏩᎧ...cow ᎠᏥᎪᏩᏘᎲ,” ᎦᏥᏲᎮᎲ. And uh....Ꮎ ᏧᎴᏅᎲ ᏓᏕᎶᏆᏍᎬ ᏃᏭ ᏍᏗ--ᎠᏎᏃ ᏱᏥᎵᏃᎮᏔᎾ ᎪᎵ,Ꭺ ᏱᎾᏛᎦ...I don’t know...ᏳᎾᏔ Ꮟ y’know ᎫᏍᏗ ᏯᏩᏛᎾ--ᎫᏍᏗ ᎾᏩᏛᏅᎾ ᏱᎨᎮ ᏱᎾᏛᎦ ᏳᏬᏂᏏ ᏳᏬᏚᏨ ᏥᎩ fluent speaker ᎡᎵᏍᏓ ᏱᏂ,ᏕᎬᏫ ᎢᎦ ᎠᎩᎸᏉᏗ ᎠᏩ,Ꮫ.ᎪᏗ
segments.translation: I think everybody should just speak their language at home and the kids will slowly pick it up. At home, that’s what they’re doing, I don’t really understand when they talk but at least they’re trying. Nan Usdi we raised her, and we always talked to her in Cherokee. When she was about three years old, she started talking Cherokee. “Ni!” she said one time when were heading to church. “There’s a cow!” she said. “What she say? What she say?” said her sisters. I told them, “She’s telling you that’s a cow she sees.” When she started school she didn’t talk—but when I talk to her she understands. I tell her to do something and she does it. I don’t know if she still knows, but I don’t have to say anything. She’ll do things at home. When she talks, it sounds pretty, cause she can make those sounds real well. I used to like to hear her talk.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᏍᎩᏍ Ᏺ’ ᏴᏩᏟᎢᎶᎦ ᎮᎵ? ᎠᏯ ᏥᏄᏍᏗ ᏥᏂᏬᏂᎲ ᏳᏍᏗ ᏴᏩᎵᎢᎶᎦ ᎮᎵ?
segments.translation: Do you think she will get back to talking like we are?

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.text: Mhm. ᎾᏛ ᏍᏊ ᏗᏂᏲᏟ ᏣᎾᏕᎶᏆᎢ...uh...ᎨᎨᏲᎲᏍᎩ Ꮳ.ᏗᎲ ᎧᎵ ᏂᎦᏪ Ꮎ “ᎣᏏᏲ” ᏣᎾᏗ...uh...ᎠᏯ ᎮᎾ, “ᏏᏲ” y’know ᎠᎯᏓᏭ ᏩᏗᏅᏗ...and uh...”ᎪᎵᎩ ᏂᏣᏛᏁᎲ,” ᏥᏲᎮᎲ Ꮎ ᎠᎨᏳᏣ After awhile ᏯᎾᎴᏅ ᎠᏃᎰᏅᏗᎲ y’know ᏥᏄᏍᏗ ᏥᏗᏬᏂ, ᏩᎴᎵ. I think so...ᎠᏎᏃ ᏙᏳ, ᎮᏅ ᎠᏁᎵᏙᏗ ᏗᎯ---ᏗᎨᏲᏗ. Oh-Ꮽ ᏌᏭ ᏳᏩᎦᏓ Dora Dunn Ꮷ--ᏗᏂᏲᏟ ᏧᎵᏏ ᎨᎲ ᏧᎾᏕᎶᏆᎥ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎠᎭᏂ ᎤᏬᏚᎯ ᏥᎩᏛ ᏥᎾᏂᏪᏍᎬ “Ꮒ,Ꮒ,Ꮒ!” ᏓᎾᏁᎶᎲᏍᎬ ᎪᎯᎦ ᎬᎩ,Ꮫ.ᎦᏅ ᎨᎲ ᏧᏂᏍᏗ ᏍᎩᏳᏍᏗ
segments.translation: The children that they are teaching, “osiyo” and just “siyo” just to say it the short way. I understand what you all are doing now, cause after awhile they will drop sounds from words. They’ll start talking like we are Waleli. I think you have to really try to learn. One time, Dora Dunn her grandkids went to school here, the kids were talking real well. “Ni, ni, ni!” when they were playing. I thought, “I haven’t heard that from little kids in a long time.”

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᎠᏯᏅ Ꮭ ᎫᏍᏗ ᏱᏕᎵᏍᎪ ᏄᏍᏛ ᎢᎦᎾᏔ ᎢᎩᏬᏂᎯᏍᏗ ᎨᎲ
segments.translation: But us, we don’t think about how we sound, we just talk.

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.text: Huh uh. But that’s...ᏍᎩᏭᏛ ᏯᏛ ᎮᏅ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎡᎵᏏ “ᏂᎪ’Ꮈ ᎮᏅ Ꭹ.Ꮆ Ᏹ.ᎵᏃᎮᏓ, ᏯᏕᏠᎦ ᎮᏅ,” ᎾᏅ Rufus Thomas you remember him? Taxi ᎠᎯᎵᏙᎯ ᏣᎳᎩᏭ ᎠᎾᏝᏃᎮᏗᎲ ᎤᏕᎶᏆᎥ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏣᏗᎮ
segments.translation: That’s just what grandma used to say, “Just talk to them all the time, and they’ll learn.” That Rufus Thomas, you remember him? He was a taxi driver, and people just talked to him in Cherokee and he learned.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: How about—I know who you’re talking about—but how about DJ Mayes?

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.translation: Does he talk too?

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: Huh uh. ᎤᏪᏥ’Ꭱ Ᏺ’ [ᏥᏴᏂᏍᏗ: Terry]. Ꮭ ᏯᏩᎾᏔ ᏃᏭ ᏄᏍᏛ ᏥᏓᏕᎶᏆᏍᎬ ᎮᏅ ᎠᎩ,-ᎠᎩ,ᏍᏓᏴᎲᏍᎩ Ꮎ ᏧᏙ ᎠᏂᏧᏣ ᎨᎢ ᏂᎪᎯᎸ ᏗᏍᏓᏩᏗᏙᎯ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏍᎩᏭ Ꮒ--ᏣᎳᎩ ᎠᏂᏬᏂᏍᎬ ᎠᏕᎶᏆᎥ ᎣᏍᏛ ᏥᎦᏬᏂᎲ
segments.translation: No, but his son [Janet: Terry], does. I don’t know how he is now, but when he was going to school he was always with my wife’s brothers. Cause they talked to him in Cherokee, he learned it, but I don’t know how he is today. He spoke real well.

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: I don’t know what he’s like today.

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.text: That’s all it’s going to take. ᏙᏳ, ᎮᏅ ᏂᎦᏓ Ꮭ ᏯᏩᎾᏔᏳ ᏥᏲᎮᎲ...uh...ᎣᎩᏃᏢ ...we... ᎣᏍᏗᏃᎮᏍᎬ ᏙᏳ, ᎣᎩᎾᎴᏅᎲ ᎺᎵᏅ ᏍᏊ ᏥᎩ “ᏣᎳᎩ ᏕᎭᏝᏃᎮᏗᎮᏍᏗ ᎠᏁ-ᎠᏂᏅ,” and she--ᎾᏛᏁᎰ ᎠᏃᎵᏥᎢ ᎮᏅᏃ ᎾᏛ ᏧᎾᏔᏂᏓ ᎨᎲ ᏌᏭ ᎤᎵᏑᏴ “Ꮭ--‘ᏗᏯᏩᎾᏔ,” ᏯᏓᏭ ᏳᏓᎭ “Ꭹ.ᎳᏛ ᏣᏚᎵᎲ ᏣᏕᎶᏆᏍᏗ ᏔᏕᎶᏆᎢ,” ᏥᏲᎮᎲ “Ꮭ ᏲᏁᎩᎭ ᏓᎬᎵᏃᎮᏔᏂ,” ᏥᏲᎮᎲ...and uh...ᏍᎩᏭᏛ ᏄᏛᏁᏗ “ᏱᏗ--ᏱᏥᏬᏂᎭ ᎠᎾᏛ.ᎩᏍᎬ ᏯᎾᏕᏠᎦ,” ᏯᏓ ᏥᎨᎲ
segments.translation: That’s all it’s gonna take, I think. Really we don’t know. I said to the person that was sitting with me, we were talking about how now we are ready and like, “Meli, talk to them in Cherokee while they’re home. They are learning now except one of the older boys, he just says “I don’t know,” when we say something. “When you decide you want to learn, you’re going to learn,” I told him. “I’m not going to talk to you in English,” I told him. “If you all would just talk Cherokee all the time, they will pick it up and learn,” she would say.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᏍᎩᎾ ᏥᏥᏃᎮᎲ Terry ᏥᏈᏍᏗ ᏴᏫ ᏯᏁᏙᎯ ᏥᎮᎲ ᏳᏓᎭᏛ Ꮎ “ᎫᏍᏗ Ꮑ-ᏂᎪᎵᎦ Ꮎ ᏲᏁᎦ ᏥᎦᏙᎬ” ᏯᎾᏗ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏂᎦᏓ ᏥᎪᎵᎪ ᎨᎲ
segments.translation: This Terry I’m talking about, we are all talking Cherokee and “This white man standing here didn’t understand anything at all,” they would say. But he understood everything!

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.translation: [laughs]

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᏧᏬᎵᏙ ᏥᎨᎲᏃ ᏱᏚᏁᏤᎸ ᎤᎵᏎᎩ ᏥᎾᎾᎵᏍᏗᎲ ᏱᏚᏁᏤᎸ
segments.translation: It was funny when he finally spoke to them, they would just turn around, surprised. They were surprised when he spoke.

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.translation: They want to learn, they learn.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: Mhmm. ᎯᎾᎲ... ..’Ꮩ ᎮᎵ ᎯᎠᏃ ᎡᎶᎯ ᏥᏄᏍᏗᏓ ‘Ꮩ--‘Ꮩ ᎤᏍᏗ ᏛᏂᎪᎢ ᎯᎠ ᎣᏂ ᏛᎾᎢ
segments.translation: Mhmm. What do you think about how the world is now? What do you think these younger kids are going to see?

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.text: ᎤᏲᏛ...ᎤᏲᏛ ᎨᎮᏍᏗ uh... ᏍᎩ ᎮᏅ ‘Ᏺ ᎠᏟᎢᎶᎯ ᎠᏩᏛ.ᏒᏪ ᎡᏚᏚ ᏄᏪᏒ ᏥᏂᎦᎵᏍᏗ ᎪᎯᎩᏅ uh...1970 ᏧᏲᎱᏒ Ꮎ ‘Ꮲ ᎠᏨᏏᏰᎥ ᎠᏓ ᏚᏲᎲ ᎣᏂ ᏥᎦᎥ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏯᏩᏝᏃᎮᏗ ᎠᎢ ᎠᏓᏙᎵᏍᏗᎲ ᏂᎪᎯᎸ ᎠᏔᏲᎯᎲ ᎣᏍᏓ uh...ᏃᏊᎴ “ᎠᏯ ᏨᎩᎵᏏ” ᏓᏓᏙᎵᏍᏗᎲ “ᏕᎱᏝᎡᏍᏗᏭ ᎣᏍᏗᏭ” and uh...ᏍᎩᏭ ᎦᏛ.ᎩᏍᎬ ᏂᎪᎯᎸ ᏃᏭ ᏯᎵᏍᏛᏡᏍᏗ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎤᏬᏂᎯᏍᏗ ᏱᎩ “ᎤᏲ ᎮᏅ ᏛᏟᎢᎶᏟ,” ᏧᏛᏅ Ꮭ ᏯᏩᎾᏔ if uh...ᎤᏁᏝᏅᎯᏭ ᏯᏁᎶᏍᏚ ᎤᏂᏁᎫᏥᏓ ᏄᎾᎵᏍᏗ ᏗᏂᏲᏟ and ᏄᎾᎾᏛᎾ ᏌᏭ ᎮᏅ Ꮎ ᏣᏂᏛ.ᏅᏍᎩ ᎫᏍᏗ Gina ᏂᎪᎯᎸ ᎠᎦ,ᏎᎯᎲ Stephanie ᎮᏅ ᏓᎵᏆ ᏣᏁᎲ ᏓᎬᏃᏎᎳᏭ but uh...I guess ᎪᎱᏍᏗ ᎤᏑᏰ ᎤᏂᏁᎴ (coughs) Ꮎ ᎤᏍᏗ ᎤᎧᏁᎲ ᏣᏥᎾᎡᎸᏅ ᏧᏛᏅ so three...ᏦᎢᏛ ᏱᏅᏓ ᎠᏪᏙᎸ ᏓᎵᏆ “ᎠᏎ ᎩᎶ ᎤᏪᏓᏍᏗ,” ᎤᎾᏛᏅ Baldore ᏓᎩᎸᏫᏍᏓᏁᎲ
segments.translation: Bad times. I grew up hearing my grandpa talk about it and it is happening now. A long time ago, 1970 he died. When he walked around outside looking for wood, I’d be walking right behind him. He would pray all the time, asking for everything to be alright and also he prayed for the grandkids. Just have them taken care of well, that’s what I would hear. He would sit down when he got to talk. “Real bad times are coming,” he would say. I don’t know if it’s God’s will why the kids are turning the way they are, they’re mean. All this stuff they’re using. Gina used to point out to me where Stephanie and them lived in Tahlequah. I’m just gonna tell you. I guess there was something in it, but they took the baby away from her. I stayed in Tahlequah for about three months, cause somebody had to stay there, they said. I was working at Baldore.

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.text: Ꮎ ᎤᏠᎩ Mike...Mike ᎤᏠᎩ ᎦᎷᎬ ᏃᏭ ᎠᏯ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏙᏍᏓᏁᏂᏓ ᏍᎩ ᏃᏍᏓᏛᏁᎲ and uh...ᏙᏳ, ᎤᎵᏎᎩᏛ ᏄᏍᏛ Ꮎ ᎠᎨᏳᏣ ᎤᏓᎾᏖᏗ ᎩᎶᎢᏭ ᏳᏓᏁᏟᏴᏒ “’Ꮩ ᏣᎵᏍᏓᏁ?” ᏥᏲᎮᎲ “ᏝᏅ ᎫᏍᏗ,” ᏯᏓᏏᏂᏙ ᏥᎨᎲ Ꮎ ᏯᏖᏃ ᏳᏛ.ᏓᏍᏗ ᎫᏍᏗ. ᎠᎦᏍᎦᏓᏁᎲ Ꮎ ᏗᏂᏲᏟ...ᏙᏳᏃ ᎬᎩᏲᏎᏛ ᎠᏩᏓᏙᎵᏍᏓᏅ ᎮᏅ ᏛᏥᎧᏁᎸ--ᏙᎨᏥᎧᏁᎸ ᏗᏂᏲᏟ....umm..Memorial Weekend ᏃᏭ ᎾᎯᏳ ᏥᏄᎵᏍᏔᏅ ᏧᏚᏅᏟᏰ Ꮷ--Ꮭ ᏯᏩᎾᏔ ᏄᎵᏍᏔᏂᏙᎸ ᎾᎯᏳ but...Ꮥ--ᏃᏊᎴ ᏙᎨᏥᏅᎡᎸ Ꮎ ᏥᏓᏳᎾᏔᏅ ᏃᏭ ᏗᏂᏲᏟ ᏝᎡ ᎠᎾᏓᏂᏘᏁᎬ “ᏥᎵᏃᎮᏗ,” ᎦᏥᏲᎮᎸ ᏙᏳ ᎠᏩᏝᏃᎮᏔᏅ “ᎠᏯ ᎤᏠᏱ ᎣᎩᎶᏒ ᏣᎩᏍᏗᎬ.,” ᏥᏲᎮᎲ “ᎮᏍᏗ ᏍᎩ ᏂᏛ.ᏁᎳ ᎯᎠ,” ᎤᏂᏠᎩ ᏁᎳᎩ ᏓᏘᏃᏢ ᎠᎭᏂ ᎠᎭᏂ ᎣᏤᏙᎲ “ᎮᏍᏗ ᏗᎾᏓᏂᎩᏍᎩ ᎤᎾᏦᏙᏗ ᏫᏘᏯᎾ,” ᎣᏍᏓ ᎤᏗᏘᎾᏫᏛᎲ ᏙᏳᏅ, ᎤᏂᏍᏓᏩᏙᏞᎡ and ᏚᎾᏘᏃᏢ ᎠᏓᏁᎸ “ᏙᎲ ᏥᏣᏚᎸ ᏍᎩ ᏣᏛᏁᏗ? ᎡᎵᏍ--ᎡᎵᏭᏍ ᏱᏍᎩᏃᎯ--ᏱᏍᎩᏃᎯᏏ ᏄᏍᏛ ᏣᎶᏒ ᏂᎯ?” ᎠᏬᎮᎸ “To this day, I’m still scarred by it,” I told her.
segments.translation: Mike’s aunt got there and would relieve me. That girl was kinda, sorta weird because she changed right away. “What’s going on with you?” I said to her. “Nothing.” She would be crawling on the floor listening to something. She was scaring the kids. So I didn’t want to, but I started praying. They brought her kids back to her. It was Memorial Weekend they had a fight, but I don’t know what happened. Then they took their kids away again. When they called me, they said they were taking the kids and I told them let me talk to her. So when I talked to them I told her I had gone through the same thing when I was young and I said, “Don’t do that to them. Tell their aunt to bring them over here. I don’t want you to put them in a police car.” They followed her here and brought the kids. “Why did you want to do that?” I told her. “Can you tell me what it was like when you grew up?” she said to me. “To this day, I’m still scarred by it,” I told her.

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.text: “ᏞᏍᏕ Ᏺ’ ᏍᎩᏳᏍᏗ ᎦᎶᎯᏍᏗ,” ᏥᏲᎮᎸ “ᏏᏓᏁᎸ Ᏹ-Ᏹ-ᏱᎨᏤᏴᏅ ᎤᏲᎢ ᎮᏅ,” ᏥᏲᎮᎲ And...uh...ᎩᎳ,...y’know ᎬᏩᏗ ᏂᏓᎦᎵᏍᏔᏂ ᏱᏂᏣᎵᏍᏓᏌ and “ᏁᎳᎩ ᎠᎭᏂ ᏓᎾᏘᏃᏢ,” ᎦᏥᏲᎮᎸ...and they did.
segments.translation: “It’s not good to go through something like this,” I told her. “When a family is taken away, it’s sad,” I told her. “This is not going to happen to you, so they can go ahead and bring the kids here,” that’s what I told her. And they did.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Is that where they grew up?

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.text: Mhm. ᏃᏭ 4 years ᎨᏥᏴᏌ ᎣᏍᏓ ᏳᎾᏛᏁᏗ
segments.translation: Yes. Now they gave them four years to do right.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: MikeᎧ ᎯᏃᎮ? Mike Sheldon ᎯᏃᎮ ᏙᎲ?
segments.translation: Mike … Mike Sheldon is that who you’re talking about?

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.translation: Yes. Mike told Stephanie “Let’s go ahead and sign the papers.”

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: For her to give the kids away?

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.text: Uh huh. “ᎮᏍᏗ ᏂᏣᏛᏁᎸᎢ” ᎠᎪᎮᎲ Ꮎ ᎠᎨᏳᏣ Gina “ᎬᏩᎦᏛ ᏙᏓᏨᏲᏌ” “No! It’s just...Ꮎ welfare Ꮣ--ᎣᎦᏕᏙ.ᏗᎲ BᏙ ᎤᎾᏛᏁᏗ ᎣᎦᏚᎵ,” ᎤᏛᏅ “ᏝᏛ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏱᎩ ᎪᏪᎵ Ꭺ-ᎪᏪᎳᏅ ᎮᏅ ᎬᏩᎦᏛ ᏙᏓᏣᏲᏏ ᏗᏂᏲᏟ,” ᏥᏲᎮᎲ--ᏣᎪᎮᎸᏛ Boy...Ꮥ-Ꭴ....ᎤᎶᏒ ᏌᏭ case worker Ꮎ Cherokee Nation “Gina, ᏁᎳᎩ ᏘᎧᎵᏏᏏ” cause ᏍᎩ ᎮᏅ ᏱᏄᎵᏍᏔᎾ ᏗᏂᏲᏟ ᏱᏚᏂᏯᏃᏞ ‘ᎸᏢ ᏗᏢ...and they wouldn’t have been together.
segments.translation: Uh huh. But they told Gina, “Don’t do that.” “They’ll let you go for the rest,” they were saying. -- “No, it’s just that the welfare people is bothering us,” Gina said. -- “We don’t want them to do that, but it’s not until you sign the papers you are going to give up the kids forever,” I told her – I mean, she was told. Boy, one of the case workers from Cherokee Nation walked by and said ,”Gina, never mind filling out the papers.” If that happened, they would’ve come and got the kids and they wouldn’t have been together.v

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: You wouldn’t have known what happened to the kids.

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.text: So Gina “ᎠᏯᏛ ᏱᏕ--ᏱᏕᏥᏴᏂ” ᎠᏯᏅ ᎨᎲ ᎠᎩ--...I guess I was getting to the old part, old age, ᏃᏭ and they thought it would be too much, and uh...Gina ᏫᏓᏥᎧᏅ ᏙᏳ, ᏍᎩᎾ ᏥᏄᎵᏍᏔᏅ ᎩᎳ ᏥᏄᎾᏛᏅ ᏄᎾᏅᏛᎾ and Stephanie ᎾᏱᏃᏢ ᎠᏭ ᏗᏢ “ᏂᎯ ᎮᏅ ᏂᏣᏯᏂᏌᏗ,” ᏣᏬᎮᎸ “No, ᎡᏣᏃᏎᎲ ᏓᎦᎶᎡᏍᏗ ᏱᏦᏪᎳᎾ ᏂᎯ ᎮᏅ ᏨᏌ ᎿᏛᎦ,” ᏙᏳ,Ꮎ...Ꭰ...ᏗᏥᎨᏳ ᎮᏅ ᎠᏂᎨᏳᏣ

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.text: and uh...it’s been about...a year. A little over a year I guess...Stephanie grocery store ᏱᏫᏥᏯᏘᏂᏓ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏧᏂᎳᏫᏍᏗ on Wednesday night, and uh...church-Ꭲ ‘Ꮲ ᏱᏫᏥᏯᏘᏂᏙ ᎠᎬᏱ ᎩᎳ ᏧᏂᎳᏫᏍᏗ...so I left early...and ᏫᏥᏯᎧᎲᏍᎬ ᏥᏯᎥ seatbelt ᏓᏩᏅᏅ ᎨᎵᎥ ᏄᏮᏅ ᏍᏊ Man! Ꮎ Robert’s Funeral Home ᏥᎪᏢ ᎥᎾᏛ ᎤᎴᏅᎲ ᎠᏮᏂᏏᎶᏍᎬ ᏂᎬ.Ꮫ ᏌᎪ.ᏂᎨ ᏥᏄᎵᏍᏔᏅ “Gah lee!” ᎨᎵᎲ ᎠᎩ.ᎿᎸᏍᏗᎲ
segments.translation: and uh...it’s been about...a year. A little over a year I guess...Stephanie grocery store yiwitsiyatinida tsigehv tsunilawisadi on Wednesday night, and uh...church-i ‘tlv yiwitsiyatinido agvyi gila tsunilawisadi...so I left early...and witsiyakahvsagv tsiyav seatbelt dawanvnv geliv nuwvnv saquu Man! na Robert’s Funeral Home tsigotlv vnadv ulenvhv awvnisilosagv nigv.dv sgo.nige tsinulisatanv “Gah lee!” gelihv agi.hnalvsadihv

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.translation: [laughs]

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.text: ᏙᏳ. Ꮩ.Ꭿ ᎠᎩᏁᏍᏗ car-Ꭲ ᎯᎠᏛ ᏥᏂᏕᎦᎵᏍᏗ...I pulled over...Ꮎ ᎮᏅ ᎬᏅᎯᏓ ᎤᏍᏘᎬ ᏥᎪᏩᏘᎲᏛ ᎦᏅᏁᏕᎬ ᏃᏭᏛ ᎯᎠ ᏂᏥᏴᏁᎸ...I would’ve broke her neck ᏂᎨᎵᎰ if I had jerked her down. ᎠᏎᏃ uh...ᏙᎯ. ᎾᏩᏛᏁᎸ “ᎡᎵᏭᏧ ᎮᎵ?” ᏥᏥᏲᎲᎸ ᎮᏅ ᏃᏭ ᏧᏕᎳᎰᏒᏅ...it was like...ᎩᎶ ᏳᏰᎢᏍᏔᏅ ᏳᏍᏗ ... ᏥᏄᏛᏁᎸ
segments.translation: There were a lot of cars, so I pulled over and with her long hair I saw it hanging, so I got hold of it. I would’ve broke her neck, I thought, if I had jerked her down, but I calmed down. And I told her, “Do you think you’ve had enough?” When she come to her senses, she acted like she just woke up. She didn’t know what she did.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: She didn’t know what she did?

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.text: No. “ᏂᎯ ᎮᏅ ᎢᎸᎯᏳ ᏓᏣᏯᎴᏏ ᎢᎸᎯᏳ ᏱᏫᏥ--ᎮᏍᏗᏅ ᏍᏊ Ꮻ.ᏒᏎᎸᎢ” ᏯᏬᏌ Ꮎ ᎤᏔᏂᏓ
segments.translation: No. “She’s gonna come and look for you, but don’t go spend the night with her!” my older son said.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᎠᏎᏅ, ᏂᎪᎯᎸ ᎮᎾ, ‘ᏓᏁᎸ ᎤᏁᏓᏍᏗ ᏥᎨᎲ Mike ᏧᎾᎵᏲᎲ
segments.translation: They used to always come to the house, her and Mike together.

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.translation: It was good.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: Yeah...um...ᏦᏍᏓᎵᎮᎵᎪ ᏦᏍᏗᎪᏛᏗᎲ ᎠᏂᎨᏳᏣ ᎤᏅᏌᏅ ᏍᏊ ᎠᎾᎵᎮᎵᎬ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏥᎦᏗᎲ ᎫᏍᏗ ᏣᎾᏛ.ᏅᏍᎬ...ᎠᏯ ᎮᏅ ᏅᎩ ᏓᏩᏓ-ᏙᏍᏓᏛ.ᎯᏍᏗ Ꮭ ᏍᏊ ᏲᎩᎾᎾᏙ. ᏙᏍᏗᎦᏴᎳᎬ ᏦᎢᏭ 3 years ago ᏥᎨᎲ ᏃᏊᎴ ᏙᏍᏗᏯᏅᏅ ᏔᏍᎩᏭ ᏓᏓᎴᏂᏍᎩ ᎠᎬᏱ ᎠᎨᏳᏣ ᏥᎨᎲ SallisawᎡ ᎤᏥ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎤᏩᏌ Ᏺ’ ᏦᎩᏂᎷᏤᎸ ᎤᏩᏌ ᏦᎩᏂᏃᏎᎴ “ᏥᏈᏍᏗ ᎮᏅ ᎫᏍᏗ ᎬᏛ.ᏅᏍᎬ Ꮭ--ᏳᏓᎭ Ꮭ ᏯᏩᎾᏙ. ᏂᎦᏛᏁᎰ ᏥᏯᏘᏂᏙᎰ ᎤᏍᏗ,” ᏧᏛᏅ ᏙᏳ ᏥᏬ--um...Ꮷ--ᏗᏁᎲ ᏥᏬᎩᏁᏙᎸ ᎦᎵᏦᏕ Ꮭ ᎫᏍᏗᏭ ᎫᏍᏗ ᎠᎵᏍᏓᏴᏗ ᏳᏂᎮ ᎠᎪᎾ ᏄᎾᏛᏁᏕᎨ “ᏍᎩᎾ ᏫᏍᏓᏘᏁᏒᎢ” ᏥᎧᏃᎮᎴ ᏙᏳᏅ, Ꮟ...uh...um...ᎠᏯ--Ꮭ--ᎦᏳᎳ ᎣᏍᏓ ᎤᏩᏌ ᎮᏅ ᏚᏓᏘᎾᎥ ᏍᏊ ᎨᎲ ᏃᏊᎴ ᏐᎢ ᎠᏧᏣ ᎤᏠᏱ Mary LouᏍ ᎯᏲᎵᎦ? ᎥᎩᏙ. ᏃᏊᎴ ᎤᎵᏏ ᎤᏍᏗᏭ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏦᎩᏂᎧᏁᎴ ᏍᎩᎾ and-and ᏃᏊᎴ ᎯᎠ-ᎯᎠ ᏦᎢ ᎾᏕᏘᏯ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏃᏊᎴ ᏔᎵ ᏙᏍᏗ--ᏂᎦᏓᏅ ᏥᏕᏂ--ᏥᏕᏥᏃᎮ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏧᎾᏓᎦᏴᎵᎨ ᎫᏍᏗ ᎠᎾᏛ.ᏅᏍᎬ ᏂᎦᎵᏍᏙᏗᏍᎨ Ꮩ-ᏙᎩᏂᎧᏁᎲ
segments.translation: We were happy to see the girls and they were happy to see us, too. Now that they’re using all these drugs. That’s what’s wrong. And we raised four kids. And we don’t even realize that we’re getting old, about three years ago we adopted two more kids. What started it, the first one was a girl from Sallisaw. It was her mom that came to us. She said she’s using too much [drugs]. “Sometimes I don’t even know what I’m doing while I’ve got the girl with me,” she said. So we went to visit at her place and they didn’t really have anything to eat there. The little girl was starving. “You all go ahead and take her,” she said. But now this girl has her own child. And the other, the boy, do you know Mary Lou Vann, my sister? She had a granddaughter that we adopted. He was little when we got him. And then three years ago we adopted two more and all these that I’m talking about, their parents were on drugs. That’s why they gave us the kids.

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.translation: That's not good.

segments.translation: Transcription not available.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᎤᏲ’Ꭱ ᏄᎵᏍᏓᏁᏛᎪᏂ ᏛᏴᏛᏁᎵ ᎮᏅ ᎨᎵ Ꮎ ᎮᏅ DHS ᏃᏭ Ꮧ-ᏦᏍᏗᎪᏛᏗᏭ ᎣᏍᏓᎵᏒᎯᎲ uh...visitation ᎣᏍᏗ--ᎣᏍᏓ--ᏚᎪᎵᏰᎥ Ꮎ ᎠᏍᎦᏯ ᎤᏩᎧᎲ ᎯᎠ ᎣᏂ ᎤᎪᎵᏰᎥᏅ ᎮᏍᏗᏅ ᏍᏊ ᏗᎦᏚᎸᎮ ᎤᏛᏁ’Ꭱ ᎥᎾᏭ ᎤᎾ--ᎤᎾ--ᎤᎾ ᎦᏳᎳ ᎤᎾᏛᏁᎵᏙᎸ ᏧᏂ--ᏧᏂᎸᏫᏍᏓᏁᎯ...um...ᏃᏭᏅ ᎤᏂᏴᏟᎦ ᎠᏂᏐᏃ “Uh, Mr. Shell, do you want ‘em?” ᏓᏬᎮᎸ ᏍᏗᏃ ᎠᏩᏓᎾᏛᎸ ᏳᏍᏗ “Yeah,” ᏩᏩᏓᏛᏁ
segments.translation: Yeah, we are in bad times, but he’s gonna do it, I think. DHS, all we wanted was to see them sometimes. Like, visitation. When that man read the papers, he said he really didn’t want the kids. The DHS did what they thought should happen. So, they came in and asked me if I wanted the kids. I guess I was crazy, I said yeah. We brought them home that evening, and they’ve been with us since. We adopted them. And all they were seeing was bad ways from their parents.

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.translation: [laughter]

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᎾᎯᏳ ᏒᎯᏰ ᏙᏍᏓᎾᏫᏛᎲ Ꮎ’Ꭱ ᏙᎩᎾᏝᏫᏍᏛ adopted ᏙᏍᏛᏁᎴ ᎠᏎᏍᎩᏂ ᏂᎦᎵᏍᏙᏗ ᎤᏲ ᎠᏂᎪᏩᏛᎯᏙᎲ ᏙᏍᏗᏯᏅᎲ ᎮᏅ...um...ᎢᏂᏍᏆᏗᏍᏗᎲᏛᏃ um...”ᎫᏍᏗ ᎠᏩᏚᎵ ᎦᏥᏃᏎᏗ Ᏸ.Ꮅ?” ‘ᎸᏍᎩ ᏄᎲ’Ꭱ ᏧᏪᏙᎸ ᎠᎨᏯ ᎣᏥᏍᏆᏗᏍᏗᎮ “Boy, ᎠᏩᏚᎵᎲ ‘ᏥᎩᎵ ᏕᏥᎪᎥ Ꮫ--ᎢᏨᏃᏎᏗ,” ᎤᏛᏅ ᎦᏳᎳ ᎣᎩᏍᏆᏛ ᎨᎲ ᎠᏎᏃ ᎯᏲᎵᎦᏅ ᏍᏊ Jenny Fletcher
segments.translation: We brought them home that evening, and they’ve been with us since. We adopted them because of all the bad they were seeing there, so we went and got them. ... We are finishing up now. You might want to tell them something—last week, a woman came and she wanted to tell us about ghosts she’d seen, but we had already finished. And you know her, Jenny Fletcher.

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.translation: [laughs]

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.text: Yeah, that girl is pretty scary.
segments.translation: Oh yeah. That girl is pretty scary.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᎠᏎᏃ...ᏙᏛ Ᏺ’ ᏙᎲ it is...uh...ᏍᎩᎾ “ᏴᏫᎨᏓ ᎮᏅ ᎣᏂ,” ᎤᏛᏅ Ᏺ’ “ᎠᏎᏭ,” ᎤᏛᏅ so...Ꮭ ᏯᏩᎾᏔ ᏱᏬᏥᏯᎾ,Ꮄ ᏱᎩ ᏱᎨᎮᏍᏗ ᏱᎩ, ᏍᎩ Ꮭ ᎫᏍᏗ ᏱᏣᏚᎵ ᏣᏃᎮᏗ ᎫᏍᏗ ᏱᎭᏅᏓᏗ?
segments.translation: Ain’t it though? She said she can come back and tell stories for free. I don’t know if we’ll call for her, or what. And you don’t wanna tell anything that you might remember?

segments.speaker: janet-navarro
segments.text: Mmm, nothing I can think of.
segments.translation: Mmm, nothing I can think of.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Alright.
